sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十】　起上章困敦十一月，盡玄黓攝提格四月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 70] From Shangzhang Kundun, the eleventh month, through Xuanyi Shetige, the fourth month; slightly more than one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 70] From Shangzhang Kundun, the eleventh month, through Xuanyi Shetige, the fourth month—slightly more than a year in all.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝中之上廣明元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Guangming, middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang, Huishèng Gongding Xiaoxiao (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Guangming (middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang) (

sentences.zh: 庚子，公元八八零年）

translations.literal: gengzi, corresponding to the year 880 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengzi, 880 CE)

sentences.zh: 十一月，河中都虞候王重榮作亂，剽掠坊市俱空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Wang Chongrong, the supervisor of the army at Hezhong, rose in rebellion; the wards and markets were plundered until entirely empty.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Wang Chongrong, army supervisor at Hezhong, rebelled and looted the wards and markets until they stood empty.

sentences.zh: 宿州刺史劉漢宏怨朝廷賞薄。

translations.literal: Liu Hanhong, prefect of Suzhou, resented that the court's rewards were meager.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong, prefect of Suzhou, resented the court's stingy rewards.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以漢宏為浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Hanhong was appointed military commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Liu Hanhong was made military commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 詔河東節度使鄭從讜以本道兵授諸葛爽及代州刺史朱玫，使南討黃巢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong military commissioner Zheng Congdang to give troops of his circuit to Zhuge Shuang and Zhu Mei, prefect of Daizhou, and send them south to attack Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hedong commissioner Zheng Congdang to detach troops from his circuit for Zhuge Shuang and Daizhou prefect Zhu Mei, and march them south against Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以代北都統李琢為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On yimao, Li Zhuo, overall commander north of Dai, was made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Li Zhuo, overall commander north of Dai, was appointed military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 初，黃巢將渡淮，豆盧瑑請以天平節鉞授巢，俟其到鎮討之，盧攜曰：「盜賊無厭，雖與之節，不能止其剽掠，不若急發諸道兵扼泗州，汴州節度使為都統，賊既前不能入關，必還掠淮、浙，偷生海渚耳。

translations.literal: Earlier, as Huang Chao was about to cross the Huai, Dou Luquan requested that the insignia of the Pingyi command be granted to Chao so that, once he reached his post, he could be dealt with. Lu Xie said, "Bandits are insatiable. Even if you give them a commission, you cannot stop their plundering. It would be better to hurry and mobilize troops from all circuits to hold Sizhou, with the Bianzhou military commissioner as supreme commander. Once the bandits cannot advance into the passes, they are sure to turn back to ravage Huai and Zhe, eking out a living on the coastal islets."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Huang Chao prepared to cross the Huai, Dou Luquan urged granting him the Pingyi command so the court could strike once he took up his post. Lu Xie objected: "Bandits know no limit. A commission will not stop their looting. Better to rush troops from every circuit to block Sizhou, with the Bianzhou commissioner as supreme commander. Denied the passes, Chao will turn back to ravage the Huai and Zhe regions and scrape a living on the coast."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court followed this counsel.

sentences.zh: 既而淮北相繼告急，攜稱疾不出，京師大恐。

translations.literal: Before long, north of the Huai, urgent reports came in one after another. Xie claimed illness and would not attend court; the capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon urgent dispatches poured in from north of the Huai. Xie pleaded illness and stayed away from court, and panic seized the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，東都奏黃巢入汝州境。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Eastern Capital reported that Huang Chao had entered the territory of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Luoyang reported that Huang Chao had crossed into Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以王重榮權知河中留後，以河中節度使同平章事李都為太子少傅。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Wang Chongrong was appointed acting regent of Hezhong, and Li Du, military commissioner of Hezhong and associate grand councilor, was made grand mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Wang Chongrong was made acting regent of Hezhong, and Li Du, Hezhong commissioner and associate grand councilor, was demoted to grand mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 汝鄭把截制置都指揮使齊克讓奏黃巢自稱天補大將軍，轉牒諸軍雲，「各宜守壘，勿犯吾鋒！

translations.literal: Qi Kerang, supreme commander of the Ruzheng interception force, reported that Huang Chao styled himself Grand General of Heavenly Succor and circulated a dispatch to the armies saying, "Each of you should hold your camps and do not cross my path!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi Kerang, supreme commander of the Ruzheng interception force, reported that Huang Chao had taken the title Grand General of Heavenly Succor and sent circulars to the armies: "Hold your positions and do not cross our path!"

sentences.zh: 吾將入東都，即至京邑，自欲問罪，無預眾人。

translations.literal: I am about to enter the Eastern Capital and will soon reach the capital. I intend to settle accounts on my own; it does not concern the rest of you.
translations.idiomatic: I am marching on Luoyang and will soon reach the capital. I mean to settle scores myself—this does not concern the rest of you.

sentences.zh: 」上召宰相議之。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned the chief ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned his chief ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 豆盧瑑、崔沆請發關內諸鎮及兩神策軍守潼關。

translations.literal: Dou Luquan and Cui Hang requested that troops from the Guannei garrisons and both Shence armies be sent to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luquan and Cui Hang urged mobilizing Guannei garrisons and both Shence armies to defend Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，日南至，上開延英，對宰要泣下。

translations.literal: On renxu, the winter solstice, the emperor opened court at Yanying Hall; facing the chief ministers' requests, he wept.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, the winter solstice, the emperor held court at Yanying Hall and wept as he faced his ministers' pleas.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使田令孜奏：「請選左右神策軍弓弩手守潼關，臣自為都指揮制置把截使。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Tian Lingzi memorialized: "Please select crossbowmen from the Left and Right Shence armies to hold Tong Pass; your servant will serve as supreme interception commander."
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Tian Lingzi proposed: "Select crossbowmen from the Left and Right Shence armies for Tong Pass, and let me serve as supreme interception commander."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「侍衛將士，不習征戰，恐未足用。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "The palace guard troops are not practiced in campaigning; I fear they will not suffice."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "The palace guards are unused to war—I doubt they will be enough."

sentences.zh: 」令孜曰：「昔安祿山構逆，玄宗幸蜀以避之。

translations.literal: " Lingzi said, "In the past An Lushan rebelled, and Emperor Xuanzong went to Shu to avoid him."
translations.idiomatic: " Lingzi said, "When An Lushan rebelled, Emperor Xuanzong withdrew to Shu to escape him."

sentences.zh: 」崔沆曰：「祿山眾才五萬，比之黃巢，不足言矣。

translations.literal: " Cui Hang said, "Lushan's force was only fifty thousand; compared with Huang Chao, he is not worth mentioning."
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Hang said, "Lushan had only fifty thousand men—beside Huang Chao he hardly counts."

sentences.zh: 」豆盧瑑曰：「哥舒翰以十五萬眾不能守潼關，今黃巢眾六十萬，而潼關又無哥舒之兵。

translations.literal: " Dou Luquan said, "Geshu Han with a hundred and fifty thousand could not hold Tong Pass. Now Huang Chao has six hundred thousand, and at Tong Pass there are no troops like Geshu's."
translations.idiomatic: " Dou Luquan said, "Geshu Han failed to hold Tong Pass with a hundred and fifty thousand. Huang Chao now fields six hundred thousand, and we have no Geshu Han at the pass."

sentences.zh: 若令孜為社稷計，三川帥臣皆令孜腹心，比於玄宗則有備矣。

translations.literal: If Lingzi were planning for the altars of state, the commanders of the Three Gorges are all his trusted men; compared with Emperor Xuanzong, he would be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: If Lingzi truly had the realm in mind, the Three Gorges commanders are all his creatures—in that respect he is better prepared than Xuanzong was.

sentences.zh: 」上不懌，謂令孜曰：「卿且為朕發兵守潼關。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased and said to Lingzi, "You, for now, raise troops for Us to hold Tong Pass."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, displeased, told Lingzi, "For now, raise troops for me to hold Tong Pass."

sentences.zh: 」是日，上幸左神策軍，親閱將士。

translations.literal: " That day the emperor visited the Left Shence army and personally reviewed the troops.
translations.idiomatic: " That day the emperor inspected the Left Shence army in person.

sentences.zh: 令孜薦左軍馬軍將軍張承范、右軍步軍將軍王師會、左軍兵馬使趙珂。

translations.literal: Lingzi recommended Zhang Chengfan, cavalry general of the Left Army; Wang Shihui, infantry general of the Right Army; and Zhao Ke, army supervisor of the Left Army.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi recommended Zhang Chengfan of the Left Army cavalry, Wang Shihui of the Right Army infantry, and Zhao Ke, Left Army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 上召見三人，以承范為兵馬先鋒使兼把截潼關制置使，師會為制置關塞糧料使，珂為句當寨柵使，令孜為左右神策軍內外八鎮及諸道兵馬都指揮制置招討等使，飛龍使楊復恭為副使。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the three men. Zhang Chengfan was made vanguard commander and Tong Pass interception commissioner; Wang Shihui, pass provisions commissioner; Zhao Ke, camp and palisade commissioner. Lingzi was made supreme commander of the Left and Right Shence armies, the eight inner and outer garrisons, and troops from all circuits; Yang Fugong, commissioner of the Flying Dragon Bureau, was made deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the three men. Zhang Chengfan became vanguard commander and Tong Pass interception commissioner; Wang Shihui, pass provisions commissioner; Zhao Ke, camp commissioner. Lingzi took supreme command of both Shence armies, eight garrisons, and all circuit forces, with Yang Fugong of the Flying Dragon Bureau as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，齊克讓奏：「黃巢已入東都境，臣收軍退保潼關，於關外置寨。

translations.literal: On guihai, Qi Kerang reported: "Huang Chao has entered the territory of the Eastern Capital. Your servant has withdrawn the army to hold Tong Pass and set up camps outside the pass."
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Qi Kerang reported: "Huang Chao has crossed into the Luoyang region. I have pulled back to Tong Pass and pitched camps outside the gate."

sentences.zh: 將士屢經戰鬥，久乏資儲，州縣殘破，人煙殆絕，東西南北不見王人，凍餒交逼，兵械刓弊，各思鄉閭，恐一旦潰去，乞早遣資糧及援軍。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers have fought repeatedly and long lacked supplies. The prefectures and counties lie in ruins; human habitation is nearly gone. In every direction one sees no agents of the throne. Cold and hunger press together; weapons are worn out. Each man longs for his home village, and I fear they will break and flee at once. I beg that provisions and reinforcements be sent soon.
translations.idiomatic: Our men have fought again and again and long gone without supplies. The prefectures lie in ruins and the land is all but deserted; nowhere does one see an agent of the throne. Cold and hunger close in, weapons are worn to nothing, and every man yearns for home—I fear they will scatter at the first shock. Send provisions and reinforcements at once.

sentences.zh: 」上命選兩神策弩手得二千八百人，令張承范等將以赴之。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered crossbowmen selected from both Shence armies, obtaining twenty-eight hundred men, and sent Zhang Chengfan and the others to lead them there.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered two thousand eight hundred Shence crossbowmen selected and sent Zhang Chengfan and the others to lead them thither.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，黃巢陷東都，留守劉允章帥百官迎謁。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Huang Chao took the Eastern Capital. Liu Yunzhang, the resident commissioner, led the hundred officials to welcome and pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Huang Chao captured Luoyang. Resident commissioner Liu Yunzhang led the officials out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 巢入城，勞問而已，閭裡晏然。

translations.literal: Chao entered the city, offered greetings and inquiries only, and the lanes and wards were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Chao entered the city, offered only courteous inquiries, and the streets remained calm.

sentences.zh: 允章，乃之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yunzhang was a great-grandson of Liu Nai.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhang was a great-grandson of Liu Nai.

sentences.zh: 田令孜奏募坊市人數千以補兩軍。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi memorialized to recruit several thousand men from the wards and markets to fill out both armies.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi proposed recruiting several thousand men from the city wards to fill both Shence armies.

sentences.zh: 辛未，陝州奏東都已陷。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Shaanzhou reported that the Eastern Capital had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Shaanzhou reported that Luoyang had fallen.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以田令孜為汝、洛、晉、絳、同、華都統，將左、右軍東討。

translations.literal: On renshen, Tian Lingzi was made overall commander of Ru, Luo, Jin, Jiang, Tong, and Hua, leading the Left and Right armies east to attack.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Tian Lingzi was made overall commander of Ru, Luo, Jin, Jiang, Tong, and Hua and marched east with both Shence armies.

sentences.zh: 是日，賊陷虢州。

translations.literal: That day the bandits took Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the rebels captured Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 以神策將羅元杲為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: The Shence general Luo Yuangao was made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shence general Luo Yuangao was appointed military commissioner of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 以周岌為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji was made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji was appointed military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 初，薛能遣牙將上蔡秦宗權調發至蔡州，聞許州亂，托雲赴難，選募蔡兵，遂逐刺史，據其城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xue Neng had sent his adjutant Qin Zongquan of Shangcai to muster troops at Caizhou. Hearing of disorder in Xuzhou, he claimed he was going to the rescue, recruited Caizhou soldiers, drove out the prefect, and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xue Neng had sent adjutant Qin Zongquan of Shangcai to raise troops at Caizhou. When Xuzhou fell into chaos, Zongquan claimed he was marching to the rescue, recruited local soldiers, expelled the prefect, and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 及周岌為節度使，即以宗權為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhou Ji became military commissioner, Zongquan was at once made prefect of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Ji took the Zhongwu commission, Zongquan was promptly made prefect of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，張承范等將神策弩手發京師。

translations.literal: On yihai, Zhang Chengfan and the others led the Shence crossbowmen out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Zhang Chengfan and the others marched the Shence crossbowmen out of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 神策軍士皆長安富家子，賂宦官竄名軍籍，厚得稟賜，但華衣怒馬，憑勢使氣，未嘗更戰陳。

translations.literal: The Shence soldiers were all sons of wealthy Chang'an families who bribed eunuchs to insert their names in the rolls, received generous stipends, wore splendid clothes and rode fierce horses, threw their weight about, and had never seen battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Shence troops were sons of Chang'an's rich who bribed eunuchs for places on the rolls, drew fat stipends, dressed splendidly and rode fine horses, bullied others by their connections, and had never seen a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 聞當出征，父子聚泣，多以金帛雇病坊貧人代行，往往不能操兵。

translations.literal: When they heard they were to campaign, fathers and sons gathered and wept. Many hired poor men from charity wards with gold and silk to go in their place, and these often could not handle weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Told they were to march, fathers and sons wept together. Many paid paupers from charity wards to take their place, and those substitutes often could not wield arms.

sentences.zh: 是日，上御章信門樓臨遣之。

translations.literal: That day the emperor went to the Zhangxin Gate tower to see them off.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor saw them off from the Zhangxin Gate tower.

sentences.zh: 承范進言：「聞黃巢擁數十萬之眾，鼓行而西，齊克讓以饑卒萬人依托關外，復遣臣以二千餘人屯於關上，又未聞為饋餉之計，以此拒賊，臣竊寒心。

translations.literal: Chengfan advanced and said, "I hear Huang Chao commands several hundred thousand men and is marching west in battle array. Qi Kerang with ten thousand starving soldiers relies on positions outside the pass, yet I am again sent with a little more than two thousand to garrison on the pass, and I have heard no plan for provisions. To resist the bandits with this—I am privately chilled at heart."
translations.idiomatic: Chengfan spoke up: "Huang Chao fields several hundred thousand and marches west in battle order. Qi Kerang holds the outside of the pass with ten thousand starving men, yet I am sent with barely two thousand atop the pass, and I hear no plan for supplies. To face the rebels like this fills me with dread."

sentences.zh: 願陛下趣諸道精兵早為繼援。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to hurry elite troops from all circuits as early reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to hurry elite troops from every circuit as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿輩第行，兵尋至矣！

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "You need only go; troops will arrive shortly!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "March on—reinforcements will follow soon!"

sentences.zh: 」丁丑，承范等至華州。

translations.literal: " On dingchou, Chengfan and the others reached Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: " On dingchou they reached Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 會刺史裴虔餘徙宣歙觀察使，軍民皆逃入華山，城中索然，州庫唯塵埃鼠跡，賴倉中猶有米千餘斛，軍士裹三日糧而行。

translations.literal: It happened that Prefect Pei Qianyu was transferred to be military commissioner of Xuanshe. Soldiers and civilians alike fled into Mount Hua. The city was desolate; the prefectural treasury held only dust and rat tracks. They relied on somewhat more than a thousand hu of rice still in the granary; the soldiers wrapped three days' rations and marched on.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Pei Qianyu had just been transferred to Xuanshe commissioner. Troops and civilians alike fled into Mount Hua, leaving the city empty and the treasury nothing but dust and rat tracks. They scraped a little over a thousand hu of rice from the granary; each man wrapped three days' grain and marched on.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚辰朔，承范等至潼關，搜菁中，得村民百許，使運石汲水，為守禦之備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the gengchen new moon, Chengfan and the others reached Tong Pass, searched the thickets, found about a hundred villagers, and had them haul stone and draw water for defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the gengchen new moon, Chengfan reached Tong Pass, rounded up about a hundred villagers from the thickets, and set them hauling stone and drawing water for the defense.

sentences.zh: 與齊克讓軍皆絕糧，士卒莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: Both their army and Qi Kerang's were out of grain; the soldiers had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies were out of grain and the men had no stomach for battle.

sentences.zh: 是日，黃巢前鋒軍抵關下，白旗滿野，不見其際。

translations.literal: That day Huang Chao's vanguard reached below the pass; white banners covered the fields with no end in sight.
translations.idiomatic: That day Chao's vanguard reached the pass; white banners blanketed the plain as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 克讓與戰，賊小卻，俄而巢至，舉軍大呼，聲振河、華。

translations.literal: Kerang fought them; the bandits fell back slightly. Soon Chao arrived; the whole army shouted, and the sound shook the Yellow River and Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang engaged them and the rebels gave ground briefly. Then Chao arrived; his whole host roared, and the sound shook the river and Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 克讓力戰，自午至酉始解，士卒饑甚，遂喧噪，燒營而潰，克讓走入關。

translations.literal: Kerang fought hard from noon until you before the engagement ended. The soldiers were very hungry; they clamored, burned their camps, and broke. Kerang fled into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang fought from noon until evening. Starving, the men raised a din, burned their camps, and fled; Kerang ran back through the pass.

sentences.zh: 關左有谷，平日禁人往來，以榷徵稅，謂之「禁坑」。

translations.literal: To the left of the pass was a ravine. Ordinarily people were forbidden to pass through it so that transit taxes could be levied; it was called the "Forbidden Ravine."
translations.idiomatic: Left of the pass lay a ravine normally closed to traffic so transit tolls could be collected—the "Forbidden Ravine."

sentences.zh: 賊至倉猝，官軍忘守之，潰兵自谷而入，谷中灌木壽籐茂密如織，一夕踐為坦塗。

translations.literal: The bandits came in haste; the government troops forgot to guard it. Routed soldiers entered by the ravine. The shrubs and long vines in the ravine were dense as woven cloth; in one night they were trampled into a level road.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came too fast; the government troops forgot the ravine. Fleeing soldiers poured through it, and in one night their feet beat the dense brush and vines into a level track.

sentences.zh: 承范盡散其輜囊以給士卒，遣使上表告急，稱：「臣離京六日，甲卒未增一人，饋餉未聞影響。

translations.literal: Chengfan distributed all his baggage to supply the soldiers and sent a messenger with an urgent memorial, stating: "Your servant left the capital six days ago; not one more armored soldier has been added, and I have heard no word of provisions."
translations.idiomatic: Chengfan gave out all his baggage to feed the men and sent an urgent memorial: "Six days out of the capital, not one more soldier has joined me, and no word of supplies has come."

sentences.zh: 到關之日，巨寇已來，以二千餘人拒六十萬眾，外軍饑潰，蹋開禁坑。

translations.literal: On the day I reached the pass, the great bandit host had already come. With a little more than two thousand I resist six hundred thousand. The outer army, starving, broke and trampled open the Forbidden Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The day I reached the pass the great rebel host was already here. I hold the pass with barely two thousand against six hundred thousand. The outer army, starving, broke and trampled open the Forbidden Ravine.

sentences.zh: 臣之失守，鼎鑊甘心。

translations.literal: If I lose the pass, I will gladly accept the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: If I lose the pass, I accept death without complaint.

sentences.zh: 朝廷謀臣，愧顏何寄！

translations.literal: As for the court's strategists—where can they hide their shame!
translations.idiomatic: As for the court's strategists—where can they hide their faces!

sentences.zh: 或聞陛下已議西巡，苟鑾輿一動，則上下土崩。

translations.literal: I have heard that Your Majesty has already discussed a western tour. If the imperial carriage moves even once, court and realm will collapse like earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Your Majesty has discussed a flight west. If the imperial carriage moves, court and realm will crumble together.

sentences.zh: 臣敢以猶生之軀奮冒死之語，願與近密及宰臣熟議，未可輕動，急徵兵以救關防，則高祖、太宗之業庶幾猶可扶持，使黃巢繼安祿山之亡，微臣勝哥舒翰之死！

translations.literal: Your servant dares with his still-living body to speak words risking death: I beg that Your Majesty deliberate thoroughly with your close attendants and chief ministers and not move lightly, but urgently summon troops to save the passes. Then the enterprise of Gaozu and Taizong might still be upheld, Huang Chao might follow An Lushan to ruin, and this humble servant would surpass Geshu Han in death!
translations.idiomatic: With my life still in me I dare speak as one facing death: deliberate long with your intimates and ministers before you move. Rush troops to save the passes, and Gaozu and Taizong's legacy may yet stand; let Huang Chao follow An Lushan to ruin, and this humble servant will have died a better death than Geshu Han!

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賊急攻潼關，承范悉力拒之，自寅及申，關上矢盡，投石以擊之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the bandits pressed the attack on Tong Pass. Chengfan resisted with all his strength from yin to shen. On the pass arrows were exhausted; they hurled stones to strike the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the rebels stormed Tong Pass. Chengfan held with all his might from dawn to mid-afternoon until arrows ran out and his men hurled stones.

sentences.zh: 關外有天塹，賊驅民千餘人入其中，掘土填之，須臾，即平，引兵而度。

translations.literal: Outside the pass was a natural moat. The bandits drove more than a thousand civilians into it to dig earth and fill it; in a moment it was level, and they led troops across.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pass lay a natural moat. The rebels drove a thousand civilians in to fill it with earth; in moments it was level and their army crossed.

sentences.zh: 夜，縱火焚關樓俱盡。

translations.literal: At night they set fires and burned all the pass towers.
translations.idiomatic: That night they burned the pass towers to the ground.

sentences.zh: 承范分兵八百人，使王師會守禁坑，比至，賊已入矣。

translations.literal: Chengfan detached eight hundred men and sent Wang Shihui to hold the Forbidden Ravine, but by the time they arrived the bandits had already entered.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfan sent Wang Shihui with eight hundred men to hold the Forbidden Ravine, but the rebels were already through when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 壬午旦，賊夾攻潼關，關上兵皆潰，師會自殺，承范變服，帥餘眾脫走。

translations.literal: At dawn on renwu the bandits attacked Tong Pass from both sides. The troops on the pass all broke. Shihui killed himself. Chengfan changed clothes and led the survivors to escape.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on renwu the rebels attacked from both sides. The garrison broke; Shihui killed himself. Chengfan changed clothes and fled with the survivors.

sentences.zh: 至野狐泉，遇奉天援兵二千繼至，承范曰：「汝來晚矣！

translations.literal: At Yehu Spring they met two thousand reinforcements from Fengtian arriving in succession. Chengfan said, "You have come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: At Yehu Spring they met two thousand Fengtian reinforcements marching up. Chengfan said, "You are too late!"

sentences.zh: 」博野、鳳翔軍還至渭橋，見所募新軍衣裘溫鮮，怒曰：「此輩何功而然，我曹反凍餒！

translations.literal: " The Boye and Fengxiang armies returned to Weiqiao Bridge and saw the newly recruited troops in warm, fresh fur and silk. In anger they said, "What merit have these men that they should be so, while we are cold and starving!"
translations.idiomatic: " The Boye and Fengxiang troops returning to Weiqiao Bridge saw the newly recruited men in warm, fresh clothing and cried, "What have they done to dress so while we freeze and starve!"

sentences.zh: 」遂掠之，更為賊鄉導，以趣長安。

translations.literal: " They thereupon plundered them, then served as guides for the bandits toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " They looted them and then guided the rebels toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 賊之攻潼關也，朝廷以前京兆尹蕭廩為東道轉運糧料使。

translations.literal: When the bandits attacked Tong Pass, the court had appointed the former metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, Xiao Lin, eastern-route transport and provisions commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Tong Pass, the court had named former Jingzhao governor Xiao Lin eastern-route transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廩稱疾，請休官，貶賀州司戶。

translations.literal: Lin claimed illness and requested retirement; he was demoted to registrar of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pleaded illness and asked to retire; he was demoted to registrar of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入華州，留其將喬鈐守之。

translations.literal: Huang Chao entered Huazhou and left his general Qiao Ling to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao entered Huazhou and left general Qiao Ling to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 河中留後王重榮請降於賊。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, regent of Hezhong, requested to surrender to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong regent Wang Chongrong offered to surrender to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 癸未，制以巢為天平節度使。

translations.literal: On guiwei, an edict appointed Chao military commissioner of Pingyi.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the court appointed Chao military commissioner of Pingyi.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以翰林學士承旨、尚書左丞王徽為戶部侍郎，翰林學士、戶部侍郎裴澈為工部侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Wang Hui, chief Hanlin academician and left vice minister of the Secretariat, was made vice minister of revenue; Pei Che, Hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, was made vice minister of works; both were appointed associate grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, chief Hanlin academician Wang Hui became vice minister of revenue and Hanlin academician Pei Che vice minister of works; both joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 以盧攜為太子賓客、分司。

translations.literal: Lu Xie was made grand mentor of the heir apparent with duties in the eastern office.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie was made grand mentor of the heir apparent and sent to the eastern office.

sentences.zh: 田令孜聞黃巢已入關，恐天子責己，乃歸罪於攜而貶之，薦徽、澈為相。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi, hearing that Huang Chao had entered the passes, feared the Son of Heaven would blame him. He shifted blame onto Xie and had him demoted, recommending Hui and Che as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, hearing Chao had broken through the passes, feared the emperor would blame him. He pinned the fault on Xie, had him demoted, and pushed Hui and Che for the council.

sentences.zh: 是夕，攜飲藥死，澈，休之從子也。

translations.literal: That evening Xie took poison and died. Che was a nephew of Pei Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Xie drank poison and died. Che was a nephew of Pei Xiu.

sentences.zh: 百官退朝，聞亂兵入城，布路竄匿，田令孜帥神策兵五百奉帝自金光門出，惟福、穆、澤、壽四王及妃嬪數人從行，百官皆莫知之。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials left court, they heard that rebel troops had entered the city and fled along every road to hide. Tian Lingzi led five hundred Shence troops escorting the emperor out through the Jinguang Gate. Only the four princes Fu, Mu, Ze, and Shou and a few consorts accompanied him; none of the officials knew.
translations.idiomatic: As officials left court they heard rebels had entered the city and scattered to hide. Tian Lingzi led five hundred Shence troops and the emperor out the Jinguang Gate with only Princes Fu, Mu, Ze, and Shou and a few consorts—no official knew.

sentences.zh: 上奔馳晝夜不息，從官多不能及。

translations.literal: The emperor galloped day and night without rest; most of his attendants could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode day and night without pause; most attendants could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 車駕既去，軍士及坊市民競入府庫盜金帛。

translations.literal: Once the imperial carriage had gone, soldiers and ward and market people rushed into the government storehouses to steal gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court had fled, soldiers and townspeople looted the government treasuries of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 晡時，黃巢前鋒將柴存入長安，金吾大將軍張直方帥文武數十人迎巢於霸上。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon, Huang Chao's vanguard general Chai Cun entered Chang'an. Zhang Zhifang, great general of the Imperial Guards, led several dozen civil and military officials to welcome Chao at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Late that afternoon Chao's vanguard general Chai Cun entered Chang'an. Imperial Guards general Zhang Zhifang led several dozen officials to welcome Chao at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 巢乘金裝肩輿，其徒皆被發，約以紅繒，衣錦繡，執兵以從，甲騎如流，輜重塞塗，千里絡繹不絕。

translations.literal: Chao rode a shoulder-borne palanquin with gold fittings. His followers all wore their hair loose, bound with red silk, dressed in brocade, and followed bearing weapons. Armored horsemen flowed like a stream; baggage blocked the roads; for a thousand li the procession was unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Chao rode a gold-trimmed palanquin. His men wore their hair loose, bound with red silk, dressed in brocade, and bore arms. Armored horsemen streamed past; baggage choked the roads for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 民夾道聚觀，尚讓歷諭之曰：「黃王起兵，本為百姓，非如李氏不愛汝曹，汝曹但安居毋恐。

translations.literal: The people lined the roads to watch. Shang Rang went along instructing them: "King Huang raised his army for the common people, not like the Li clan who did not love you. You need only live in peace and do not fear."
translations.idiomatic: Crowds lined the roads. Shang Rang told them: "King Huang took up arms for the people, not like the Li house that cared nothing for you. Stay at home and do not fear."

sentences.zh: 」巢館於田令孜第，其徒為盜久，不勝富，見貧者，往往施與之。

translations.literal: " Chao lodged at Tian Lingzi's mansion. His followers had long been bandits; unable to bear such wealth, when they saw the poor they often gave to them.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao lodged in Tian Lingzi's mansion. Long accustomed to robbery, his men, overwhelmed by wealth, often gave alms to the poor.

sentences.zh: 居數日，各出大掠，焚市肆，殺人滿街，巢不能禁。

translations.literal: After several days each went out on great looting raids, burned the markets, and killed until the streets were full of corpses; Chao could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: After a few days they sallied out to loot on a grand scale, burned the markets, and filled the streets with the dead; Chao could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 尤憎官吏，得者皆殺之。

translations.literal: They especially hated officials; any they caught they killed.
translations.idiomatic: They hated officials above all and killed every one they caught.

sentences.zh: 上趣駱谷，鳳翔節度使鄭畋謁上於道次，請車駕留鳳翔。

translations.literal: The emperor hurried through Luogu Valley. Zheng Tian, military commissioner of Fengxiang, met the emperor on the road and asked that the imperial carriage remain at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed through Luogu Valley. Fengxiang commissioner Zheng Tian met him on the road and begged him to stay at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕不欲密邇巨寇，且幸興元，徵兵以圖收復。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "We do not wish to stay close to the great bandit. For now We shall go to Xingyuan and raise troops to plan recovery."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will not lodge near the great rebel. I go to Xingyuan to raise troops and plan recovery."

sentences.zh: 卿東扞賊鋒，西撫諸蕃，糾合鄰道，勉建大勳。

translations.literal: You, eastward, hold the bandits' spearpoint; westward, pacify the various barbarians; gather the neighboring circuits and strive to build great merit."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the rebel spearhead in the east, pacify the western tribes, rally the neighboring circuits, and strive for great merit."

sentences.zh: 」畋曰：「道路梗澀，奏報難通，請得便宜從事。

translations.literal: " Tian said, "The roads are blocked and reports hard to send. I beg leave to act as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: " Tian said, "The roads are blocked and dispatches will not get through. I beg discretion to act as need requires."

sentences.zh: 」許之，戊子，上至婿水，詔牛勖、楊師立、陳敬瑄，諭以京城不守，且幸興元，若賊勢猶盛，將幸成都，宣豫為備擬。

translations.literal: " This was granted. On wuzi the emperor reached Xu River and issued edicts to Niu Xu, Yang Shili, and Chen Jingxuan, informing them that the capital could not be held, that for now he would go to Xingyuan, and that if the bandits' strength remained great he would go to Chengdu; Xuan and Yu were to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: " This was granted. On wuzi he reached Xu River and notified Niu Xu, Yang Shili, and Chen Jingxuan that the capital was lost, that he was bound for Xingyuan, and that if the rebels still held sway he would go on to Chengdu; Xuan and Yu were to prepare accordingly.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，黃巢殺唐宗室在長安者無遺類。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Huang Chao killed every member of the Tang imperial clan in Chang'an without exception.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Huang Chao slaughtered every Tang imperial clansman in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，巢始入宮。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Chao for the first time entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Chao entered the palace for the first time.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，巢即皇帝位於含元殿，畫皁繒為袞衣，擊戰鼓數百以代金石之樂。

translations.literal: On renchen, Chao took the imperial throne in Hanyuan Hall, painted black silk for his robe, and beat several hundred war drums in place of metal and stone music.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Chao took the throne in Hanyuan Hall, wore robes of painted black silk, and beat hundreds of war drums in place of ritual music.

sentences.zh: 登丹鳳樓，下赦書。

translations.literal: He ascended the Danfeng Tower and issued an amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted Danfeng Tower and proclaimed an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 國號大齊，改元金統。

translations.literal: The state was named Great Qi, and the era name was changed to Jintong.
translations.idiomatic: He named his state Great Qi and adopted the era name Jintong.

sentences.zh: 謂廣明之號，去唐下體而著黃家日月，以為己符瑞。

translations.literal: He said that in the era name Guangming, the lower element of Tang was removed and the sun and moon of the Huang house were displayed, taking this as his own omen.
translations.idiomatic: He read the era name Guangming as stripping Tang's lower element to reveal the Huang house's sun and moon—a sign that the mandate was his.

sentences.zh: 唐官三品以上悉停任，四品以下位如故。

translations.literal: Tang officials of the third rank and above were all suspended; those of the fourth rank and below kept their posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: All Tang officials of third rank and above were dismissed; fourth rank and below kept their posts.

sentences.zh: 以妻曹氏為皇后。

translations.literal: His wife, the Cao clan, was made empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife, Lady Cao, empress.

sentences.zh: 以尚讓為太尉兼中書令，趙璋兼侍中，崔璆、楊希古並同平章事，孟楷、蓋洪為左右僕射、知左右軍事，費傳古為樞密使。

translations.literal: Shang Rang was made grand marshal and director of the Secretariat; Zhao Zhang was also made chief steward; Cui Qiu and Yang Xigu were both made associate grand councilors; Meng Kai and Gai Hong were left and right vice directors and overseers of left and right military affairs; Fei Chuanggu was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang became grand marshal and Secretariat director; Zhao Zhang, chief steward; Cui Qiu and Yang Xigu, associate grand councilors; Meng Kai and Gai Hong, vice directors overseeing left and right forces; Fei Chuanggu, military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以太常博士皮日休為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Pi Rixiu, doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Rixiu, doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 璆，邠之子也，時罷浙東觀察使，在長安，巢得而相之。

translations.literal: Qiu was a son of Cui Bin. At the time he had been dismissed as military commissioner of Zhedong and was in Chang'an; Chao seized him and made him chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was Cui Bin's son, lately dismissed from Zhedong and still in Chang'an; Chao took him for chief minister.

sentences.zh: 諸葛爽以工北行營兵頓櫟陽，黃巢將碭山朱溫屯東渭橋，巢使溫誘說之，爽遂降於巢。

translations.literal: Zhuge Shuang led the northern campaign army of the engineering corps and encamped at Liyang. Huang Chao's general Zhu Wen of Dangshan held Dongwei Bridge. Chao sent Wen to persuade him, and Shuang thereupon surrendered to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Shuang camped at Liyang with the northern campaign army. Chao's general Zhu Wen of Dangshan held Dongwei Bridge and persuaded him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 溫少孤貧，與兄昱、存隨母王氏依蕭縣劉崇家，崇數笞辱之，崇母獨憐之，戒家人曰：「朱三非常人也，汝曹善遇之。

translations.literal: Wen in youth was orphaned and poor. With his elder brothers Yu and Cun he followed his mother, the Wang clan, to live with the Liu Chong family of Xiao County. Chong often beat and humiliated him, but Chong's mother alone pitied him and warned the household: "Zhu the Third is no ordinary man; you should treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: Wen was orphaned and poor. With brothers Yu and Cun he lived with his mother at Liu Chong's house in Xiao County. Chong often beat him, but Chong's mother pitied him and warned the family: "Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—treat him kindly."

sentences.zh: 」巢以諸葛爽為河陽節度使，爽赴鎮，羅元杲發兵拒之，士卒皆棄甲迎爽，元杲逃奔行在。

translations.literal: " Chao made Zhuge Shuang military commissioner of Heyang. Shuang went to his post; Luo Yuangao raised troops to resist him, but the soldiers all cast off their armor to welcome Shuang. Yuangao fled to the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao made Shuang Heyang commissioner. When Shuang marched to his post, Luo Yuangao resisted, but the troops cast off armor to welcome Shuang and Yuangao fled to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋還鳳翔，召將佐議拒賊，皆曰：「賊勢方熾，且宜從容以俟兵集，乃圖收復。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian returned to Fengxiang, summoned his officers to discuss resisting the bandits, and all said, "The bandits' power is at its height; for now we should proceed calmly, wait for troops to gather, and then plan recovery."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian returned to Fengxiang and asked his officers about resisting the rebels. All said the rebels were at their peak and they should wait for troops to gather before planning recovery.

sentences.zh: 」畋曰：「諸君勸畋臣賊乎！

translations.literal: " Tian said, "Are you gentlemen urging Tian to serve the bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: " Tian cried, "Are you urging me to serve the rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」因悶絕仆地，甃傷其面，自午到明旦，尚未能言。

translations.literal: " He thereupon fainted and fell, injuring his face on the brick floor. From noon until dawn the next day he still could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " He fainted and struck his face on the bricks. From noon until dawn he could not speak.

sentences.zh: 會巢使者以赦書至，監軍彭敬柔與將佐序立宣示，代畋草表署名以謝巢。

translations.literal: It happened that Chao's envoy arrived with the amnesty edict. Army supervisor Peng Jingrou and the officers stood in order to proclaim it and, in Tian's stead, drafted a memorial and signed to thank Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's envoy arrived with the amnesty. Supervisor Peng Jingrou and the officers read it aloud and, for Tian, drafted a thank-you memorial to Chao.

sentences.zh: 監軍與巢使者宴，樂奏，將佐以下皆哭。

translations.literal: The army supervisor feasted with Chao's envoy. When music played, the officers and all below wept.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor feasted the envoy. When music played, every officer wept.

sentences.zh: 使者怪之，幕客孫儲曰：「以相公風痺不能來，故悲耳。

translations.literal: The envoy was puzzled. Staff member Sun Chu said, "Because the chief minister's wind ailment keeps him from coming, they grieve."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was puzzled. Staff member Sun Chu said, "They grieve because the chief minister's paralysis keeps him away."

sentences.zh: 」民間聞者無不泣。

translations.literal: " None who heard it among the people failed to weep.
translations.idiomatic: " Every commoner who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 畋聞之曰：「吾固知人心尚未厭唐，賊授首無日矣！

translations.literal: When Tian heard this he said, "I have long known that hearts have not yet turned from Tang. The day the bandits lose their heads is not far!"
translations.idiomatic: Tian heard and said, "I knew hearts had not yet forsaken Tang. The rebels' end is near!"

sentences.zh: 」乃刺指血為表，遣所親間道詣行在，召將佐諭以逆順，皆聽命，復刺血與盟，然後完城塹，繕器械，訓士卒，密約鄰道合兵討賊，鄰道皆許諾發兵，會於鳳翔。

translations.literal: " He then pricked his finger and wrote a memorial in blood, sent a close follower by secret route to the imperial procession, summoned his officers to instruct them on loyalty and treason, and all obeyed. He again drew blood to covenant with them, then repaired walls and moats, readied weapons, trained soldiers, and secretly arranged with neighboring circuits to combine forces against the bandits. The neighboring circuits all promised to send troops and assemble at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote a blood memorial and sent a trusted man by secret route to the emperor. He rallied his officers on loyalty and treason, sealed the pact in blood, repaired defenses, trained troops, and secretly enlisted neighboring circuits to join at Fengxiang—all promised troops.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍分鎮關中兵尚數萬，聞天子幸蜀，無所歸，畋使人招之，皆往從畋，畋分財以結其心，軍勢大振。

translations.literal: At the time the palace troops garrisoned in Guanzhong still numbered tens of thousands. Hearing the Son of Heaven had gone to Shu and with nowhere to go, Tian sent men to recruit them; all came to follow Tian. Tian distributed wealth to win their hearts, and military strength greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of palace troops still garrisoned Guanzhong. Hearing the emperor had fled to Shu, they had nowhere to go; Tian recruited them all, paid them generously, and his army swelled.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，車駕至興元，詔諸道各出全軍收復京師。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the imperial carriage reached Xingyuan. An edict ordered each circuit to send its full army to recover the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the court reached Xingyuan and ordered every circuit to march its full strength to recover the capital.

sentences.zh: 己亥，黃巢下令，百官詣趙璋第投名銜者，復其官。

translations.literal: On jihai, Huang Chao ordered that officials who went to Zhao Zhang's residence to submit their name plaques would have their offices restored.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Chao ordered that officials who registered at Zhao Zhang's residence would regain their posts.

sentences.zh: 豆盧瑑、崔沆及左僕射-{于}-琮、右僕射劉鄴、太子少師裴諗、御史中丞趙水蒙、刑部侍郎李溥、京兆尹李湯扈從不及，匿民間，巢搜獲，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Dou Luquan, Cui Hang, and the left vice director Yu Cong, right vice director Liu Ye, grand mentor of the heir apparent Pei Shen, imperial censor Zhao Shuimeng, vice minister of justice Li Pu, and metropolitan governor of Jingzhao Li Tang failed to keep up with the imperial procession, hid among the people, were searched out and seized by Chao, and all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luquan, Cui Hang, left vice director Yu Cong, right vice director Liu Ye, grand mentor Pei Shen, censor Zhao Shuimeng, vice minister Li Pu, and Jingzhao governor Li Tang could not keep pace, hid among the people, were found by Chao, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 廣德公主曰：「我唐室之女，誓與於僕射俱死！

translations.literal: Princess Guangde said, "I am a daughter of the Tang house and swear to die together with Vice Director Yu!"
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guangde declared, "I am Tang's daughter and swear to die with Vice Director Yu!"

sentences.zh: 」執賊刃不置，賊並殺之。

translations.literal: " She seized a bandit blade and would not let go; the bandits killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: " She seized a rebel blade and would not release it; the rebels killed them both.

sentences.zh: 發盧攜屍，戮之於市。

translations.literal: Lu Xie's corpse was exhumed and displayed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie's corpse was dug up and exposed in the market.

sentences.zh: 將作監鄭綦、庫部郎中鄭系義不臣賊，舉家自殺。

translations.literal: Director of Palace Construction Zheng Qi and bureau director Zheng Xi, refusing to serve the bandits on principle, killed their whole families and themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Palace construction director Zheng Qi and bureau director Zheng Xi, refusing to serve the rebels, killed their entire families.

sentences.zh: 左金吾大將軍張直方雖臣於巢，多納亡命，匿公卿於復壁。

translations.literal: Left great general of the Imperial Guards Zhang Zhifang, though he had submitted to Chao, took in many fugitives and hid high officials in secret chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Left Imperial Guards general Zhang Zhifang had submitted to Chao but sheltered fugitives and hid officials in secret rooms.

sentences.zh: 巢殺之。

translations.literal: Chao killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chao had him killed.

sentences.zh: 初，樞密使楊復恭薦處士河間張濬，拜太常博士，遷度支員外郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yang Fugong had recommended the recluse Zhang Jun of Hejian, who was appointed doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to assistant director of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, military affairs commissioner Yang Fugong had recommended recluse Zhang Jun of Hejian, who became a Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctor and then assistant revenue director.

sentences.zh: 黃巢逼潼關，濬避亂商山。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao pressed Tong Pass, Jun fled the turmoil to Shangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao threatened Tong Pass, Jun fled to Shangshan.

sentences.zh: 上幸興元，道中無供頓，漢陰令李康以騾負糗糧數百馱獻之，從行軍士始得食。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Xingyuan, there were no supply stations on the road. Magistrate Li Kang of Hanyin presented several hundred packloads of grain carried on mules; only then did the marching soldiers get food.
translations.idiomatic: On the road to Xingyuan there were no supply stations. Hanyin magistrate Li Kang sent hundreds of mule-loads of grain, and the marching troops ate at last.

sentences.zh: 上問康：「卿為縣令，何能如是？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Kang, "As a county magistrate, how could you do this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Kang, "As a county magistrate, how could you manage this?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣不及此，乃張濬員外教臣。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant did not reach this on his own; it was Assistant Director Zhang Jun who taught me."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I could not have done it alone—Assistant Director Zhang Jun taught me."

sentences.zh: 」上召濬詣行在，拜兵部郎中。

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Jun to the imperial procession and appointed him director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor summoned Jun and made him director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使王處存聞長安失守，號哭累日，不俟詔命，舉軍入援，遣二千人間道詣興元衛車駕。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun, military commissioner of Yiwu, hearing that Chang'an had fallen, wailed for many days. Without waiting for an edict, he raised his whole army to aid the court and sent two thousand men by secret route to Xingyuan to guard the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu commissioner Wang Chucun wailed for days when Chang'an fell. Without waiting for orders he marched to the rescue and sent two thousand men by secret route to guard the emperor at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 黃巢遣使調發河中，前後數百人，吏民不勝其苦。

translations.literal: Huang Chao sent envoys to levy requisitions in Hezhong; several hundred came in succession, and officials and people could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent envoys to levy Hezhong again and again—hundreds in all—and officials and commoners were crushed.

sentences.zh: 王重榮謂眾曰：「始吾屈節以紓軍腐之患，今調財不已，又將徵兵，吾亡無日矣！

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong said to the assembly, "At first I humbled myself to relieve the army's exactions; now levies of wealth never cease and troops will be drafted again. My death is not far off!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong told the troops, "I submitted at first to ease the army's exactions, but levies never stop and they will draft troops again—I am as good as dead!"

sentences.zh: 不如發兵拒之。

translations.literal: It would be better to raise troops and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to raise troops and resist.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆以為然，乃悉驅巢使者殺之。

translations.literal: " All thought this right, and they drove out all of Chao's envoys and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: " All agreed, drove out Chao's envoys, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 巢遣其將朱溫自同州，弟黃鄴自華州，合兵擊河中，重榮與戰，大破之，獲糧仗四十餘船，遣使與王處存結盟，引兵營於渭北。

translations.literal: Chao sent his general Zhu Wen from Tongzhou and his brother Huang Ye from Huazhou to combine forces and attack Hezhong. Chongrong fought them and inflicted a great defeat, capturing grain and weapons on more than forty boats. He sent envoys to ally with Wang Chucun and led troops to encamp north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Zhu Wen from Tongzhou and his brother Huang Ye from Huazhou against Hezhong. Chongrong routed them, took forty-odd boatloads of grain and arms, allied with Wang Chucun, and camped north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄聞車駕出幸，遣步騎三千奉迎，表請幸成都。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan, hearing the imperial carriage had departed, sent three thousand infantry and cavalry to welcome it and memorialized asking that the court go to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the court had fled, Chen Jingxuan sent three thousand troops to welcome it and asked that the emperor come to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 時從兵浸多，興元儲偫不豐，田令孜亦功上。

translations.literal: At the time the following troops steadily increased, stores at Xingyuan were not ample, and Tian Lingzi also urged the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The retinue kept growing, Xingyuan's stores ran thin, and Tian Lingzi also urged the emperor on.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝中之上中和元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Zhonghe, middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang, Huishèng Gongding Xiaoxiao (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Zhonghe (middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang) (

sentences.zh: 辛丑，公元八八一年）

translations.literal: xinchou, corresponding to the year 881 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinchou, 881 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，車駕發興元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the imperial carriage departed Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the court left Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 加牛勖同平章事。

translations.literal: Niu Xu was made associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Xu joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄以扈從之人驕縱難制，有內園小兒先至成都，游於行宮，笑曰：「人言西川是蠻，今日觀之，亦不惡！

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan found the entourage arrogant and hard to control. An inner-park pageboy reached Chengdu first, wandered about the traveling palace, and laughed, "People say western Shu is barbarian country—seeing it today, it is not so bad!"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan found the entourage unruly. A palace pageboy reached Chengdu first, toured the traveling palace, and laughed, "They say western Shu is barbarian land—today it does not look so bad!"

sentences.zh: 」敬瑄執而杖殺之，由是眾皆肅然。

translations.literal: " Jingxuan seized him and beat him to death; from this the crowd all became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingxuan seized and flogged him to death, and thereafter all were subdued.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄迎謁於鹿頭關。

translations.literal: Jingxuan welcomed and paid homage at Lutou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan welcomed the court at Lutou Pass.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上至綿州，東川節度使楊師立謁見。

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor reached Mianzhou; Yang Shili, military commissioner of Dongchuan, paid homage.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor reached Mianzhou; Dongchuan commissioner Yang Shili paid homage.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以工部侍郎、判度支蕭遘同平章事。

translations.literal: On renshen, Xiao Gou, vice minister of works and acting director of revenue, was made associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, vice minister of works Xiao Gou, acting revenue director, joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋約前朔方節度使田弘夫、涇原節度使程宗楚同討黃巢。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian arranged with the former military commissioner of Shuofang, Tian Hongfu, and the military commissioner of Jingyuan, Cheng Zongchu, to attack Huang Chao together.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian enlisted former Shuofang commissioner Tian Hongfu and Jingyuan commissioner Cheng Zongchu to attack Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 巢遣其將王暉繼詔召畋，畋斬之，遣其子凝績詣行在，凝績追及上於漢州。

translations.literal: Chao sent his general Wang Hui with a forged edict summoning Tian. Tian beheaded him and sent his son Ningji to the imperial procession; Ningji caught up with the emperor at Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent general Wang Hui with a forged summons. Tian beheaded him and sent his son Ningji to the emperor; Ningji caught up at Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，車駕至成都，館於府捨。

translations.literal: On dingchou the imperial carriage reached Chengdu and lodged in the prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the court reached Chengdu and lodged in the prefectural compound.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使趣高駢討黃巢，道路相望，駢終不出兵。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoys to urge Gao Pian to attack Huang Chao; they filled the roads one after another, but Pian in the end would not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys one after another urging Gao Pian to attack Chao, but Pian never marched.

sentences.zh: 上至蜀，猶冀駢立功，詔駢巡內刺史及諸將有功者，自監察至常侍，聽以墨敕除訖奏聞。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Shu he still hoped Pian would achieve merit and ordered that within Pian's circuit, prefects and generals with merit, from surveillance commissioner through regular attendant, might be appointed by informal edict and reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shu, the emperor still hoped Pian would serve and authorized him to appoint officials from surveillance commissioner through regular attendant by informal edict, reporting afterward.

sentences.zh: 裴澈自賊中奔詣行在。

translations.literal: Pei Che fled from the bandits to the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Che escaped the rebels to join the emperor.

sentences.zh: 時百官未集，乏人草制，右拾遺樂朋龜謁田令孜而拜之，由是擢為翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred officials had not yet assembled and there was no one to draft edicts. Remonstrance official Yue Penggui visited Tian Lingzi and bowed to him; for this he was promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: With officials not yet assembled and no one to draft edicts, remonstrance official Yue Penggui bowed to Tian Lingzi and was made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 張濬先稱亦拜令孜。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun had also announced he would bow to Lingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had likewise announced he would bow to Lingzi.

sentences.zh: 令孜嘗召宰相及朝貴飲酒，濬恥於眾中拜令孜，乃先謁令孜，謝酒。

translations.literal: Lingzi once summoned the chief ministers and court nobles to drink. Jun was ashamed to bow to Lingzi before the crowd, so he first visited Lingzi privately to decline the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi once summoned ministers and nobles to drink. Jun, ashamed to bow in public, visited Lingzi beforehand to decline.

sentences.zh: 及賓客畢集，令孜言曰：「令孜與張郎中清濁異流，嘗蒙中外，既慮玷辱，何憚改更，今日於隱處謝酒則又不可。

translations.literal: When all guests were assembled, Lingzi said, "Lingzi and Director Zhang are of different streams, pure and turbid. I was once honored inside and outside the palace. Fearing disgrace, why shrink from changing? Yet today to decline wine in private is again impossible."
translations.idiomatic: When all had gathered, Lingzi said, "Director Zhang and I move in different worlds. I was once honored at court. If he fears disgrace, why not change openly? Declining wine in private will not do."

sentences.zh: 」濬慚懼無所容。

translations.literal: " Jun was ashamed and afraid, with nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun was mortified and had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙卯朔，以太子少師王鐸守司徒兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the yimao new moon, Wang Duo, grand mentor of the heir apparent, was made acting grand marshal and chief steward and associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the yimao new moon, grand mentor Wang Duo became acting grand marshal, chief steward, and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 丙申，加鄭畋同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Zheng Tian was made associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zheng Tian joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 加淮南節度使高駢東面都統，加河東節度使鄭從讜兼侍中，依前行營招討使。

translations.literal: Gao Pian, military commissioner of Huainan, was made eastern overall commander; Zheng Congdang, military commissioner of Hedong, was also made chief steward, continuing as former camp pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan commissioner Gao Pian became eastern overall commander; Hedong commissioner Zheng Congdang was also made chief steward and kept his pacification post.

sentences.zh: 代北監軍陳景思帥沙陀酋長李友金及薩葛、安慶、吐谷渾諸部入援京師。

translations.literal: Chen Jingsi, army supervisor north of Dai, led the Shatuo chief Li Youjin and the Sige, Anqing, and Tuyuhun tribes to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dai army supervisor Chen Jingsi led Shatuo chief Li Youjin and Sige, Anqing, and Tuyuhun tribes toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 至絳州，將濟河。

translations.literal: They reached Jiangzhou and were about to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Jiangzhou and prepared to cross the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 絳州刺史瞿稹，亦沙陀也，請景思曰：「賊勢方盛，未可輕進，不若且還代北募兵。

translations.literal: Qu Zhi, prefect of Jiangzhou, was also Shatuo. He asked Jingsi, "The bandits' power is at its height; we must not advance lightly. Better to return north of Dai for now and recruit troops."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou prefect Qu Zhi, also Shatuo, urged Jingsi, "The rebels are at their peak—do not advance rashly. Better return north of Dai and recruit."

sentences.zh: 」遂與景思俱還雁門。

translations.literal: " They then returned to Yanmen together with Jingsi.
translations.idiomatic: " They returned to Yanmen together.

sentences.zh: 以樞密使楊復光為京城西南面行營都監。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made overall supervisor of the southwestern capital-area campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs commissioner Yang Fuguang became overall supervisor of the southwestern capital-area campaign.

sentences.zh: 黃巢以朱溫為東南面行營都虞候，將兵攻鄧州。

translations.literal: Huang Chao made Zhu Wen eastern-area army supervisor and sent him with troops to attack Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chao made Zhu Wen eastern-area army supervisor and sent him against Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥，陷之，執刺史趙戎，因戍鄧州以扼荊、襄。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinhai, he took it, seized Prefect Zhao Rong, and garrisoned Dengzhou to choke Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinhai, he captured it, seized prefect Zhao Rong, and garrisoned Dengzhou to block Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，加陳敬瑄同平章事。

translations.literal: On renzi, Chen Jingxuan was made associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Chen Jingxuan joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，敬瑄奏遣左黃頭軍使李鋋將兵擊黃巢。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Jingxuan memorialized sending Li Xian of the Left Yellow-Head Army to lead troops against Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Jingxuan proposed sending Li Xian of the Left Yellow-Head Army against Chao.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以鄭畋為京城四面諸軍行營都統。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Zheng Tian was made overall commander of the capital-area armies on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Zheng Tian became overall commander of all capital-area armies.

sentences.zh: 賜畋詔：「凡蕃、漢將士赴難有功者，並聽以墨敕除官。

translations.literal: An edict was granted to Tian: "All barbarian and Han officers and soldiers who come to the rescue with merit may be appointed to office by informal edict."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Tian, "All Han and non-Han troops who serve with merit may be appointed by informal edict."

sentences.zh: 」畋奏以涇原節度使程宗楚為副都統，前朔方節度使唐弘夫為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: " Tian memorialized making Cheng Zongchu, military commissioner of Jingyuan, deputy overall commander, and Tang Hongfu, former military commissioner of Shuofang, campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " Tian named Jingyuan commissioner Cheng Zongchu deputy commander and former Shuofang commissioner Tang Hongfu campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 黃巢遣其將尚讓、王播帥眾五萬寇鳳翔，畋使弘夫伏兵要害，自以兵數千，多張旗幟，疏陳於高岡。

translations.literal: Huang Chao sent his generals Shang Rang and Wang Bo with fifty thousand men to raid Fengxiang. Tian had Hongfu set ambushes at critical points and himself took several thousand troops, displaying many banners in loose formation on the high ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Chao sent Shang Rang and Wang Bo with fifty thousand against Fengxiang. Tian hid Hongfu in ambush and himself deployed several thousand with many banners on the heights.

sentences.zh: 賊以畋書生，輕之，鼓行而前，無復行伍，伏發，賊大敗於龍尾陂，斬首二萬餘級，伏屍數十里。

translations.literal: The bandits thought Tian a mere scholar and despised him. They advanced in battle array without keeping ranks. The ambush struck; the bandits suffered a great defeat at Longwei Slope. More than twenty thousand heads were taken; corpses lay for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels despised the scholar Tian, marched carelessly, and were ambushed. At Longwei Slope more than twenty thousand were killed; corpses stretched for miles.

sentences.zh: 有書尚書省門為詩以嘲賊者，尚讓怒，應在省官及門卒，悉抉目倒懸之；

translations.literal: Someone wrote a poem mocking the bandits on the Ministry of Personnel gate. Shang Rang was furious. All officials on duty in the ministry and gate guards had their eyes gouged out and were hung upside down;
translations.idiomatic: Someone posted a mocking poem on the Personnel Ministry gate. Shang Rang had every official on duty and every gate guard blinded and hung upside down;

sentences.zh: 大索城中能為詩者，盡殺之；

translations.literal: a thorough search was made in the city for anyone who could write poetry, and all were killed;
translations.idiomatic: everyone in the city who could write poetry was hunted down and killed;

sentences.zh: 識字者給賤役。

translations.literal: those who could read were assigned menial duties.
translations.idiomatic: the literate were given menial labor.

sentences.zh: 凡殺三千餘人。

translations.literal: In all more than three thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand died in all.

sentences.zh: 瞿稹，李友金至代州，募兵逾旬，得三萬人，皆北方雜胡，屯於崞西，獷悍暴橫，稹與友金不能制。

translations.literal: Qu Zhi and Li Youjin reached Daizhou, recruited for more than ten days, and obtained thirty thousand men, all northern mixed barbarians encamped west of Guo. Fierce, brutal, and overbearing, they could not be controlled by Zhi and Youjin.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhi and Li Youjin raised thirty thousand northern tribesmen west of Guo—fierce and ungovernable.

sentences.zh: 友金乃說陳景思曰：「今雖有眾數萬，苟無威望之將以統之，終無成功。

translations.literal: Youjin then persuaded Chen Jingsi, "Though we now have tens of thousands, without a commander of prestige to lead them, we will never succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Youjin told Chen Jingsi, "Tens of thousands mean nothing without a commander of prestige."

sentences.zh: 吾兄司徒父子，勇略過人，為眾所服。

translations.literal: My elder brother the grand marshal and his son surpass others in courage and strategy and are obeyed by the masses."
translations.idiomatic: My brother the grand marshal and his son excel in courage and are trusted by all."

sentences.zh: 驃騎誠奏天子赦其罪，召以為帥，則代北之人一麾響應，狂賊不足平也！

translations.literal: If Your Honor truly memorializes the Son of Heaven to pardon their crimes and summons them as commander, then the people north of Dai will respond at a wave of the hand, and the mad bandits will be nothing to pacify!"
translations.idiomatic: If you seek an imperial pardon and summon them as commander, all north of Dai will answer, and the rebels will fall!"

sentences.zh: 」景思以為然，遣使詣行在言之。

translations.literal: " Jingsi thought this right and sent an envoy to the imperial procession to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingsi agreed and sent word to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔如所請。

translations.literal: An edict followed the request.
translations.idiomatic: The court assented.

sentences.zh: 友金以五百騎繼詔詣達靼迎之，李克用帥靼諸部萬人赴之。

translations.literal: Youjin with five hundred cavalry followed the edict to the Tartar lands to welcome him. Li Keyong led ten thousand men of the Tartar tribes to come.
translations.idiomatic: Youjin rode five hundred cavalry to the Tartar lands with the pardon. Li Keyong came with ten thousand tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 群臣追從車駕者稍稍集成都，南北司朝者近二百人。

translations.literal: The chief ministers who had followed the imperial carriage gradually gathered at Chengdu; nearly two hundred from the northern and southern bureaus attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who had followed the court gradually gathered at Chengdu; nearly two hundred northern and southern officials attended.

sentences.zh: 諸道及四夷貢獻不絕，蜀中府庫充實，與京師無異。

translations.literal: Tributes from the circuits and the four barbarians did not cease; the treasuries of Shu were full, no different from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tributes from circuits and foreign states flowed in; Shu's treasuries were as full as the capital's.

sentences.zh: 賞賜不乏，士卒欣悅。

translations.literal: Rewards were not lacking and the soldiers were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were generous and the troops rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 黃巢得王徽，逼以官，徽陽瘖，不從。

translations.literal: Huang Chao seized Wang Hui and pressed an office on him. Hui feigned muteness and would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chao seized Wang Hui and pressed office on him. Hui feigned muteness and refused.

sentences.zh: 月餘，逃奔河中，遣人間道奉絹表詣行在。

translations.literal: After more than a month he fled to Hezhong and sent a man by secret route with a silk memorial to the imperial procession.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he fled to Hezhong and sent a secret memorial to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔以徽為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: An edict made Hui minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Hui minister of war.

sentences.zh: 前夏綏節度使諸葛爽復自河陽奉表自歸，即以為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: The former military commissioner of Xia-Sui, Zhuge Shuang, again submitted a memorial of self-return from Heyang and was at once made military commissioner of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Former Xia-Sui commissioner Zhuge Shuang submitted again from Heyang and was restored as Heyang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宥州刺史拓跋思恭，本党項羌也，糾合夷、夏兵會鄜延節度使李孝昌於鄜州，同盟討賊。

translations.literal: Tuo Ba Sigong, prefect of Youzhou, was originally of the Tangut Qiang; he gathered barbarian and Han troops and joined Fuyan military commissioner Li Xiaochang at Fuzhou, swearing alliance to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ba Sigong, prefect of Youzhou, was a Tangut Qiang by origin. He mustered both tribal and Chinese forces, joined Fuyan military commissioner Li Xiaochang at Fuzhou, and entered an alliance to campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 奉天鎮使齊克儉遣使詣鄭畋求自效。

translations.literal: Qi Kejian, commissioner of the Fengtian garrison, sent an envoy to Zheng Tian to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Kejian, commander of the Fengtian garrison, dispatched an envoy to Zheng Tian offering to serve the cause.

sentences.zh: 甲子，畋傳檄天下籓鎮，合兵討賊。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Tian circulated a proclamation to all the military commissioners throughout the realm, calling for combined forces to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, Zheng Tian issued a call to arms to every regional command, summoning united forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時天子在蜀，詔令不通，天下謂朝廷不能復振，及得畋檄，爭發兵應之。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven was in Shu; imperial edicts could not reach the realm, and the world believed the court could not recover; when Tian's proclamation arrived, all vied to raise troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then in Shu, and court orders no longer reached the provinces. Many had concluded that the dynasty could not rise again—until Zheng Tian's proclamation arrived and commands across the land scrambled to answer it with troops.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，不敢復窺京西。

translations.literal: The bandits were afraid and dared not again watch for an opportunity in the lands west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, alarmed, no longer dared probe the approaches to Chang'an from the west.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊寅朔，加王鐸兼侍中。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day of the month, wuyin, Wang Duo was given the additional title of Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the new moon of wuyin, Wang Duo was additionally appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以拓跋思恭權知夏綏節度使。

translations.literal: Tuo Ba Sigong was made acting military commissioner of Xia-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Ba Sigong was appointed acting military commissioner of Xia-Sui.

sentences.zh: 黃巢以其將王玫為邠寧節度使，邠州通塞鎮將朱玫起兵誅之，讓別將李重古為節度使，自將兵討巢，是時，唐弘夫屯渭北，王重榮屯沙苑，王處存屯渭橋，拓跋思恭屯武功，鄭畋屯盩厔。

translations.literal: Huang Chao made his general Wang Mei military commissioner of Binning; Zhu Mei, garrison commander at Tongsa in Bin Prefecture, raised troops and executed him, had another officer Li Chonggu made military commissioner, and personally led troops against Chao. At that time Tang Hongfu was stationed north of the Wei, Wang Chongrong at Shayuan, Wang Chucun at Weiqiao, Tuo Ba Sigong at Wugong, and Zheng Tian at Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had appointed his general Wang Mei military commissioner of Binning. Zhu Mei, garrison commander at Tongsa in Bin Prefecture, rose up, killed Wang Mei, installed another officer, Li Chonggu, in the post, and marched against Chao in person. Tang Hongfu was then encamped north of the Wei River, Wang Chongrong at Shayuan, Wang Chucun at Weiqiao, Tuo Ba Sigong at Wugong, and Zheng Tian at Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 弘夫乘龍尾之捷，進薄長安。

translations.literal: Hongfu, riding the victory at Longwei, advanced close to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Buoyed by his victory at Longwei Slope, Tang Hongfu pressed toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 壬午，黃巢帥眾東走，程宗楚先自延秋門入，弘夫繼至，處存帥銳卒五千夜入城。

translations.literal: On renwu, Huang Chao led his masses east in flight; Cheng Zongchu first entered through Yanqiu Gate, Hongfu followed, and Chucun led five thousand picked troops into the city by night.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Huang Chao fled east with his army. Cheng Zongchu entered first through Yanqiu Gate; Hongfu arrived next, and Wang Chucun led five thousand elite soldiers into the city under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 坊市民喜，爭歡呼出迎官軍，或以瓦礫擊賊，或拾箭以供官軍。

translations.literal: The ward and market people rejoiced, vying to shout and come out to welcome the government troops; some threw tiles and stones at the bandits, others picked up arrows to supply the government army.
translations.idiomatic: People in the wards and markets erupted in joy, rushing out to greet the imperial troops with cheers. Some pelted the rebels with bricks and rubble; others gathered fallen arrows for the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 宗楚等恐諸將分其功，不報鳳翔、鄜夏，軍士釋兵入第捨，掠金帛、妓妾。

translations.literal: Zongchu and the others, fearing the other generals would share their credit, did not report to Fengxiang and Fuxia; the soldiers threw down their weapons, entered private residences, and plundered gold, silk, and courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful that other commanders might claim a share of the glory, Zongchu and his allies failed to notify the Fengxiang and Fuxia forces. Their troops threw aside their arms, stormed private homes, and looted gold, silk, and concubines.

sentences.zh: 處存令軍士首系白{須巾}為號，坊市少年或竊其號以掠人。

translations.literal: Chucun ordered his soldiers to tie white headcloths on their heads as a mark; young men of the wards and markets sometimes stole this mark to plunder people.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun had his men wear white headcloths as identification, but street youths sometimes copied the badge to rob civilians.

sentences.zh: 賊露宿霸上，詗知官軍不整，且諸軍不相繼，引兵還襲之，自諸門分入，大戰長安中，宗楚、弘夫死，軍士重負不能走，是以甚敗，死者什八九。

translations.literal: The bandits bivouacked in the open at Bashang; they learned that the government army was not in order and that the various forces did not follow one another in succession; they led troops back to strike, entering separately through the various gates, and fought a great battle within Chang'an; Zongchu and Hongfu died; the soldiers, heavily laden, could not flee; therefore the defeat was very severe, and eight or nine tenths of them died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had camped in the open at Bashang. Learning that the imperial forces were disorganized and that no units were backing one another up, they wheeled about, re-entered the city through multiple gates, and fought through Chang'an. Zongchu and Hongfu were killed; soldiers weighed down with loot could not escape. The rout was catastrophic—eight or nine soldiers in ten perished.

sentences.zh: 處存收餘眾還營。

translations.literal: Chucun gathered the remnant troops and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun rallied what was left of his force and withdrew to camp.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，巢復入長安，怒民之助官軍，縱兵屠殺，流血成川，謂之洗城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Chao re-entered Chang'an; angered that the people had aided the government army, he let his troops massacre; blood flowed like rivers—it was called "cleansing the city."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Chao reoccupied Chang'an. Furious that the populace had aided the imperial army, he unleashed a wholesale massacre. Blood ran in streams—a slaughter remembered as "washing the city."

sentences.zh: 於是諸軍皆退，賊勢愈熾。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the armies retreated, and the bandits' power grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: All imperial forces fell back, and rebel strength surged anew.

sentences.zh: 賊所署同州刺史王溥、華州刺史喬謙、商州刺史宋巖聞巢棄長安，皆率眾奔鄧州，朱溫斬溥、謙，釋巖，使還商州。

translations.literal: Wang Pu, prefect of Tongzhou appointed by the bandits, Qiao Qian, prefect of Huazhou, and Song Yan, prefect of Shangzhou, hearing that Chao had abandoned Chang'an, all led their troops to flee to Dengzhou; Zhu Wen executed Pu and Qian, released Yan, and sent him back to Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu of Tongzhou, Qiao Qian of Huazhou, and Song Yan of Shangzhou—all Huang Chao's appointees—heard that he had abandoned Chang'an and fled with their troops toward Dengzhou. Zhu Wen executed Pu and Qian, spared Yan, and sent him back to Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，拓跋思恭、李孝昌與賊戰於王橋，不利。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Tuo Ba Sigong and Li Xiaochang fought the bandits at Wangqiao and fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Tuo Ba Sigong and Li Xiaochang met the rebels at Wangqiao and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔以河中留後王重榮為節度使。

translations.literal: An edict made Wang Chongrong, acting regent of Hezhong, military commissioner of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, deputy military governor of Hezhong, was formally appointed military commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 賊眾上黃巢尊號曰承天應運啟聖睿文宣武皇帝。

translations.literal: The bandit masses elevated Huang Chao with the honorific title Emperor of Grand Accomplishment, Heavenly Compliance, Fortunate Beginning, Sagely Wisdom, Civil and Martial Excellence Who Upholds Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel host enthroned Huang Chao under the grand title "Emperor Who Receives Heaven, Aligns with Destiny, Opens the Sage Age, and Embodies Sagely Letters and Martial Valor."

sentences.zh: 有雙雉集廣陵府捨，占者以為野鳥來集，城邑將空之兆，高駢惡之，乃移檄四方，雲將入討黃巢，悉發巡內兵八萬，舟二千艘，旌旗甲兵甚盛。

translations.literal: A pair of pheasants alighted on the mansion of the prefecture at Guangling; diviners took it as an omen that wild birds gathering meant a city would be emptied; Gao Piao loathed this; he then circulated a proclamation to the four quarters, declaring he would enter to attack Huang Chao, mustering all troops within his circuit—eighty thousand soldiers, two thousand boats—with banners, armor, and weapons in great display.
translations.idiomatic: Two pheasants settled on the Guangling prefectural headquarters. Augurs read this as the classic omen of wild birds foretelling a deserted city—a sign Gao Piao found ominous. He issued proclamations in every direction announcing a campaign against Huang Chao, mobilizing eighty thousand circuit troops and two thousand ships in a show of banners, armor, and arms.

sentences.zh: 五月，己未，出屯東塘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiwei, he went out and encamped at Dongtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the fifth month, he marched out and encamped at Dongtang.

sentences.zh: 諸將數請行期，駢托風濤為阻，或雲時日不利，竟不發。
