translations.literal: The generals repeatedly asked for a date to march; Piao pleaded that wind and waves blocked the way, or that the day and hour were unfavorable—and in the end did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates pressed repeatedly for a departure date. Piao cited stormy seas, then inauspicious astrological timing—and never sailed.

sentences.zh: 李克用牒河東，稱奉詔將兵五萬討黃巢，令具頓遞，鄭從讜閉城以備之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent a dispatch to Hedong, stating that by imperial order he was leading fifty thousand troops against Huang Chao and ordering preparations for supplies and relay stations; Zheng Congyan closed the city to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong notified Hedong that he was marching fifty thousand men against Huang Chao by imperial order and demanded relay supplies. Zheng Congyan shut Taiyuan's gates against him.

sentences.zh: 克用屯於汾東，從讜犒勞，給其資糧，累日不發。

translations.literal: Keyong encamped east of the Fen River; Congyan treated his army with rewards and supplied provisions, yet for many days did not let them depart.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong camped east of the Fen. Congyan feasted his army and sent provisions—but kept them idle for days.

sentences.zh: 克用自至城下大呼，求與從讜相見，從讜登城謝之。

translations.literal: Keyong personally came beneath the walls and shouted loudly, asking to meet Congyan face to face; Congyan mounted the wall and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong rode to the foot of the walls and shouted for a meeting. Congyan appeared atop the battlements and apologized.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，復求發軍賞給，從讜以錢千緡、米千斛遺之。

translations.literal: On guihai, he again asked for rewards and supplies for the army's departure; Congyan sent him one thousand strings of cash and one thousand bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he demanded marching pay. Congyan sent a thousand strings of cash and a thousand bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 甲子，克用縱沙陀剽掠居民，城中大駭。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Keyong let the Shatuo plunder the people; great terror arose within the city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Keyong's Shatuo troops looted the city, spreading panic.

sentences.zh: 從讜求救於振武節度使契苾璋，璋引突厥、吐谷渾救之，破沙陀兩寨，克用追戰至晉陽城南，璋引兵入城，沙陀掠陽曲、榆次而歸。

translations.literal: Congyan sought rescue from Qibi Zhang, military commissioner of Zhenwu; Zhang led Turks and Tuyuhun to save them, broke two Shatuo camps; Keyong pursued the battle to the south of Jinyang city; Zhang led his troops into the city; the Shatuo plundered Yangqu and Yuci and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan appealed to Zhenwu commissioner Qibi Zhang, who marched in with Turk and Tuyuhun auxiliaries, smashed two Shatuo camps, and fought Keyong to the southern walls of Jinyang before retreating into the city. Keyong's men looted Yangqu and Yuci on their way out.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之克長安也，忠武節度使周岌降之。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao captured Chang'an, Zhou Ji, military commissioner of Zhongwu, submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang'an, Zhongwu military commissioner Zhou Ji surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 岌嘗夜宴，急召監軍楊復光，左右曰：「周公臣賊，將不利於內侍，不可往。

translations.literal: Ji once held an evening banquet and urgently summoned the army supervisor Yang Fuguang; those around him said, "Lord Zhou serves the bandits—he may mean harm to the eunuch supervisor; you must not go."
translations.idiomatic: One night at a feast Ji urgently summoned army supervisor Yang Fuguang. His attendants warned, "Lord Zhou has submitted to the rebels—he may mean you harm. Do not go."

sentences.zh: 」復光曰：「事已如此，義不圖全。

translations.literal: Fuguang said, "Things have come to this; righteousness does not plan for self-preservation."
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang replied, "Matters have reached this pass. Honor leaves no room for self-preservation."

sentences.zh: 」即詣之。

translations.literal: He at once went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，岌言及本朝，復光泣下，良久，曰：「丈夫所感者，恩義耳！

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, Ji spoke of the dynasty; Fuguang wept; after a long while he said, "What a true man is moved by is grace and duty!"
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed, Ji spoke of loyalty to the dynasty. Fuguang wept. At length he said, "What moves a true man is gratitude and obligation!"

sentences.zh: 公自匹夫為公侯，奈何捨十八葉天子而臣賊乎！

translations.literal: "You rose from a common man to duke and marquis—how can you abandon an eighteen-generation Son of Heaven to serve bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: "You rose from common birth to noble rank—how can you abandon an emperor of eighteen generations to serve rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」岌亦流涕曰：「吾不能獨拒賊，故貌奉而心圖之。

translations.literal: Ji also shed tears and said, "I could not oppose the bandits alone, so I feigned submission while plotting in my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji wept as well. "I could not stand alone against the rebels, so I bowed outwardly while plotting in secret."

sentences.zh: 今日召公，正為此耳。

translations.literal: "Today I summoned you precisely for this."
translations.idiomatic: "I summoned you tonight for exactly this purpose."

sentences.zh: 」因瀝酒為盟。

translations.literal: Thereupon they poured wine as a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: They sealed the pact with wine.

sentences.zh: 是夕，復光遣其養子守亮殺賊使者於驛。

translations.literal: That same night Fuguang sent his adoptive son Shouliang to kill the bandit envoy at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: That night Fuguang's adopted son Shouliang murdered the rebel envoy at the relay station.

sentences.zh: 時秦宗權據蔡州，不從岌命，復光將忠武兵三千詣蔡州，說宗權同舉兵討巢。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Zongquan held Cai Prefecture and did not obey Ji's orders; Fuguang led three thousand Zhongwu troops to Cai Prefecture to persuade Zongquan to join in raising troops against Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan held Cai Prefecture and ignored Zhou Ji's orders. Fuguang marched three thousand Zhongwu troops there to enlist him in the campaign against Chao.

sentences.zh: 宗權遣其將王淑將兵三千從復光擊鄧州，逗留不進，復光斬之，並其軍，分忠武八千人為八都，遣牙將鹿晏弘、晉暉、王建、韓建、張造、李師泰、龐從等八人將之。

translations.literal: Zongquan sent his general Wang Shu to lead three thousand troops to follow Fuguang in attacking Deng Prefecture; Shu delayed and would not advance; Fuguang executed him, merged his army, divided eight thousand Zhongwu troops into eight commands, and dispatched the adjutant generals Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Wang Jian, Han Jian, Zhang Zao, Li Shitai, Pang Cong, and seven others to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan sent Wang Shu with three thousand men to join Fuguang against Dengzhou. Shu stalled. Fuguang executed him, absorbed his force, split eight thousand Zhongwu soldiers into eight battalions, and assigned Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Wang Jian, Han Jian, Zhang Zao, Li Shitai, Pang Cong, and four other adjutants to lead them.

sentences.zh: 王建，舞陽人；

translations.literal: Wang Jian was a man of Wuyang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian was from Wuyang;

sentences.zh: 韓建，長社人；

translations.literal: Han Jian was a man of Changshe;
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian was from Changshe;

sentences.zh: 晏弘、暉、造、師泰，皆許州人也。

translations.literal: Yanhong, Hui, Zao, and Shitai were all men of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanhong, Jin Hui, Zhang Zao, and Li Shitai were all from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 復光帥八都與朱溫戰，敗之，遂克鄧州，逐北至藍橋而還。

translations.literal: Fuguang led the eight commands to fight Zhu Wen, defeated him, then captured Deng Prefecture, pursued north to Lanqiao, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang led the eight battalions against Zhu Wen, routed him, took Dengzhou, chased the enemy north to Lanqiao, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使高潯會王重榮攻華州，克之。

translations.literal: Gao Xun, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, joined Wang Chongrong in attacking Huazhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi commissioner Gao Xun joined Wang Chongrong in an assault on Huazhou and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊戌，以鄭畋為司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事，都統如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuxu, Zheng Tian was made Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor; his post as overall commander remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the sixth month, Zheng Tian was appointed Grand Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Grand Councilor, while retaining his post as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 李克用遇大雨，己亥，引兵北還，陷忻、代二州，因留居代州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong encountered heavy rain; on jihai he led his troops back north, captured Xin and Dai Prefectures, and remained stationed at Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was caught in heavy rains. On jihai he marched north, seized Xin and Dai prefectures, and settled at Dai.

sentences.zh: 鄭從讜遣教練使論安等軍百井以備之。

translations.literal: Zheng Congyan sent drill instructor Lun An and troops to Baijing to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Congyan dispatched drill instructor Lun An with troops to Baijing to block Keyong's advance.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度副使朱玫屯興平，黃巢將王播圍興平，玫退屯奉天及龍尾陂。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei, deputy military commissioner of Binning, was encamped at Xingping; Huang Chao's general Wang Bo besieged Xingping; Mei retreated and encamped at Fengtian and Longwei Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Binning deputy commissioner Zhu Mei was encamped at Xingping when Huang Chao's general Wang Bo besieged the city. Zhu Mei withdrew to Fengtian and Longwei Slope.

sentences.zh: 西川黃頭軍使李鋌將萬人，鞏鹹將五千人屯興平，為二寨，與黃巢戰，屢捷。

translations.literal: Li Chen, commissioner of the Yellow-Head Army of Xichuan, led ten thousand men; Gong Xian led five thousand and encamped at Xingping in two camps; they fought Huang Chao and won repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chen of the Xichuan Yellow-Head Army commanded ten thousand men; Gong Xian led five thousand. They established two camps at Xingping, clashed with Huang Chao's forces, and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄遣神機營使高仁厚將二千人益之。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan sent Shenji Camp commissioner Gao Renhou to lead two thousand men to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan sent Shenji Camp commander Gao Renhou with two thousand reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，改元，赦天下。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, the reign era was changed and an amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingsi, the dynasty changed the reign title and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎韋昭度同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Minister of War Wei Zhaodu was made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Minister of War Wei Zhaodu was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 論安自百井擅還，鄭從讜不解靴衫斬之，滅其族。

translations.literal: Lun An arbitrarily returned from Baijing on his own authority; Zheng Congyan, without removing his boots and robe, executed him and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun An withdrew from Baijing without authorization. Zheng Congyan executed him on the spot—boots and official robes still on—and wiped out his entire family.

sentences.zh: 更遣都頭溫漢臣將兵屯百井。

translations.literal: He then sent commandant Wen Hanchen to lead troops and encamp at Baijing.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Lun An with commandant Wen Hanchen, stationed at Baijing.

sentences.zh: 契苾璋引兵還振武。

translations.literal: Qibi Zhang led his troops back to Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Zhang withdrew his forces to Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 初，車駕至成都，蜀軍賞錢人三緡。

translations.literal: Initially, when the imperial carriage arrived at Chengdu, each Sichuan soldier was rewarded three strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the court first reached Chengdu, each local Sichuan soldier received three strings of cash as a reward.

sentences.zh: 田令孜為行在都指揮處置使，每四方貢金帛，輒頒賜從駕諸軍無虛月，不復及蜀軍，蜀軍頗有怨言。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi served as overall commander and disposal officer of the mobile court; whenever tribute of gold and silk arrived from the four quarters, he distributed it to the armies accompanying the emperor every month without fail, no longer extending to the Sichuan troops—the Sichuan army had considerable grievances.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, chief commander of the refugee court, distributed tribute gold and silk monthly to every unit that had followed the emperor—but never to the Sichuan garrison. Resentment festered among the local troops.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，令孜宴土客都頭，以金盃行酒，因賜之，諸都頭皆拜而受，西川黃頭軍使郭琪獨不受，起言曰：「諸將月受俸料，豐贍有餘，常思難報，豈敢無厭！

translations.literal: On bingyin, Lingzi feasted the commandants of local and guest troops, circulated wine in golden cups, and bestowed them as gifts; all the commandants bowed and accepted, but Guo Qi, commissioner of the Yellow-Head Army of Xichuan, alone refused; he rose and said, "The generals receive monthly salary allowances, ample and more than sufficient—we always think how hard it is to repay this; how would we dare be insatiable!"
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Tian Lingzi banqueted the local and visiting commandants, passing wine in golden cups and presenting the cups as gifts. Every commandant bowed and accepted—except Guo Qi of the Yellow-Head Army. He stood and declined: "We already receive generous monthly pay and rations. We can scarcely repay such favor—how could we be greedy for more!"

sentences.zh: 顧蜀軍與諸軍同宿衛，而賞賚懸殊，頗有觖望，恐萬一致變。

translations.literal: "Yet the Sichuan army guards alongside the other armies, while rewards and gifts differ greatly—a considerable sense of resentment; I fear that in the worst case there may be a mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet our Sichuan troops stand the same guard duty as the rest, while rewards are wildly unequal. Resentment runs deep—I fear it may spark rebellion."

sentences.zh: 願軍容減諸將之賜以均蜀軍，使土客如一，則上下幸甚！

translations.literal: "I wish the Army Supervisor would reduce the gifts to the other generals to equalize the Sichuan army, so that local and guest troops are the same—then above and below would be greatly fortunate!"
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Lordship would trim the other commanders' bonuses to level the field with us, so local and visiting troops were treated alike, the whole camp would be grateful!"

sentences.zh: 」令孜默然有間，曰：「汝嘗有何功？

translations.literal: Lingzi was silent for a while, then said, "What merit have you ever had?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi fell silent. At last he asked, "What deeds have you ever performed?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「琪生長山東，征戍邊鄙，嘗與党項十七戰，契丹十餘戰，金創滿身。

translations.literal: He replied, "I grew up in Shandong, campaigning on the frontier; I fought the Tangut seventeen times and the Khitan more than ten times; wounds cover my body."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qi answered, "I grew up in the east, soldiering on the frontier. I have fought the Tangut seventeen times and the Khitan more than ten. My body is a map of scars."

sentences.zh: 又嘗征吐谷渾，傷脅腸出，線縫復戰。

translations.literal: "I also once campaigned against the Tuyuhun; a wound tore open my flank and intestines protruded; I was sewn with thread and returned to battle."
translations.idiomatic: "Once against the Tuyuhun, a wound tore open my side and spilled my intestines. I was sewn up and went back to the fight."

sentences.zh: 」令孜乃自酌酒於別樽以賜琪。

translations.literal: Lingzi then poured wine himself into a separate cup and bestowed it on Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi poured wine into a separate cup and offered it to Guo Qi.

sentences.zh: 琪知其毒，不得已，再拜飲之。

translations.literal: Qi knew it was poisoned; having no choice, he bowed twice and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qi knew it was poisoned. He had no choice but to bow twice and drink.

sentences.zh: 歸，殺一婢，吮其血以解毒，吐黑汁數升，遂帥所部作亂，丁卯，焚掠坊市。

translations.literal: On returning he killed a maidservant, sucked her blood to counteract the poison, vomited several sheng of black fluid, then led his command in revolt; on dingmao he burned and plundered the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Back at camp he killed a servant girl and drank her blood to draw out the toxin, vomiting gallons of black bile. He then led his troops in revolt. On dingmao they torched and looted the city wards.

sentences.zh: 令孜奉天子保東城，閉門登樓，命諸軍擊之。

translations.literal: Lingzi escorted the Son of Heaven to secure the eastern city, closed the gates, mounted the tower, and ordered the various armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi hurried the emperor into the eastern city, barred the gates, mounted the watchtower, and ordered all units to strike.

sentences.zh: 琪引兵還營，陳敬瑄命都押牙安金山將兵攻之，琪夜突圍出，奔廣都，從兵皆潰，獨廳吏一人從，息於江岸。

translations.literal: Qi led his troops back to camp; Chen Jingxuan ordered the chief adjutant An Jinshan to lead troops to attack him; Qi broke out of the encirclement by night and fled to Guangdu; his followers all scattered; only one clerical officer of the command accompanied him; they rested on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qi withdrew to camp. Chen Jingxuan sent chief adjutant An Jinshan after him. Guo Qi broke out by night, fled to Guangdu, and lost his army—all but one clerk who stayed with him. They rested on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 琪謂廳吏曰：「陳公知吾無罪，然軍府掠擾，不可以莫之安也。

translations.literal: Qi said to the clerical officer, "Lord Chen knows I am innocent, yet with the military headquarters plundering, there cannot be peace without an accounting."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qi told the clerk, "Lord Chen knows I am guiltless, but the commandery is in uproar. Order cannot be restored without a reckoning."

sentences.zh: 汝事吾能始終，今有以報汝。

translations.literal: "You have served me to the end; now I have a way to repay you."
translations.idiomatic: "You have stood by me to the end. Now I can repay you."

sentences.zh: 汝繼吾印劍詣陳公曰：『郭琪走渡江，我以劍擊之，墜水，屍隨湍流下矣。

translations.literal: "You take my seal and sword and go to Lord Chen and say: 'Guo Qi fled across the river; I struck him with a sword; he fell into the water; his corpse was carried downstream by the current."
translations.idiomatic: "Take my seal and sword to Lord Chen and tell him: 'Guo Qi fled across the river. I struck him with my sword. He fell into the water and his body was swept downstream.'"

sentences.zh: 得其印劍以獻。

translations.literal: "Present the seal and sword you obtained."
translations.idiomatic: "Bring his seal and sword as proof."

sentences.zh: 」陳公必據汝所言，榜懸印劍於市以安眾。

translations.literal: "Lord Chen is sure to act on your word, post a placard, and hang the seal and sword in the market to reassure the people."
translations.idiomatic: "Chen will take you at your word, post the seal and sword in the marketplace, and calm the city."

sentences.zh: 汝當獲厚賞，吾家亦保無恙。

translations.literal: "You will receive a rich reward, and my family will also be kept safe."
translations.idiomatic: "You will win a rich reward, and my family will be spared."

sentences.zh: 吾自此適廣陵，歸高公，後數日，汝可密以語吾家也。

translations.literal: "From here I will go to Guangling and return to Lord Gao; after a few days you may secretly tell my family."
translations.idiomatic: "I will make for Guangling and seek shelter with Lord Gao. In a few days, send word privately to my family."

sentences.zh: 」遂解印劍授之而逸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he removed the seal and sword, handed them over, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He handed over seal and sword and disappeared.

sentences.zh: 廳吏以獻敬瑄，果免琪家。

translations.literal: The clerical officer presented them to Jingxuan, and indeed Qi's family was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk did as instructed. Guo Qi's family was spared.

sentences.zh: 上日夕專與宦官同處，議天下事，待外臣殊疏薄。

translations.literal: The emperor by day and night consorted exclusively with eunuchs to discuss affairs of the realm, treating outer court officials with exceptional coldness and distance.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the emperor kept company only with eunuchs, deliberating on state affairs; he treated the outer court with open disdain.

sentences.zh: 庚午，左拾遺孟昭圖上疏，以為：「治安之代，遐邇猶應同心；

translations.literal: On gengwu, Left Remonstrator Meng Zhaotu submitted a memorial, stating: "In an age of peace and order, near and far should still act with one heart;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Left Remonstrator Meng Zhaotu memorialized the throne: "Even in peaceful times, court and provinces must stand as one.

sentences.zh: 多難之時，中外尤當一體。

translations.literal: in times of many hardships, inner and outer courts should especially be a single body."
translations.idiomatic: In crisis, that unity is all the more essential between palace and bureaucracy."

sentences.zh: 去冬車駕西幸，不告南司，遂使宰相、僕射以下悉為賊所屠，獨北司平善。

translations.literal: Last winter when the imperial carriage went west, the southern offices were not informed, with the result that grand councilors, vice directors, and all below were slaughtered by the bandits, while only the northern offices remained unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter, when the court fled west, the southern offices—that is, the civil bureaucracy—were never warned. Grand councilors, vice directors, and their colleagues were butchered by the rebels, while the northern offices—the eunuch establishment—emerged unscathed.

sentences.zh: 況今朝臣至者，皆冒死崎嶇，遠奉君親，所宜自茲同休等戚。

translations.literal: Moreover, the court officials who have now arrived all risked death through perilous paths to serve the ruler and parent from afar—they should from this point share fortune and grief alike.
translations.idiomatic: Those civil officials who have now rejoined the court risked death on hazardous roads to reach their sovereign. Henceforth they deserve to share the dynasty's fortunes and sorrows as equals.

sentences.zh: 伏見前夕黃頭軍作亂，陛下獨與令孜、敬瑄及諸內臣閉城登樓，並不召王鐸已下及收朝臣入城。

translations.literal: "I observe that on the night before last when the Yellow-Head Army rebelled, Your Majesty alone with Lingzi, Jingxuan, and the various inner officials closed the gates and mounted the tower, neither summoning Wang Duo and those below nor admitting court officials into the city."
translations.idiomatic: "When the Yellow-Head Army mutinied the night before last, Your Majesty sealed the eastern quarter with Tian Lingzi, Chen Jingxuan, and the inner eunuchs alone atop the wall. Wang Duo and the other ministers were neither summoned nor admitted into the refuge."

sentences.zh: 翌日，又不對宰相，亦不宣慰朝臣。

translations.literal: The next day, again there was no audience with the grand councilors, nor any words of reassurance to the court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The next day brought no audience for the grand councilors, no words of reassurance for the court.

sentences.zh: 臣備位諫官，至今未知聖躬安否，況疏冗乎！

translations.literal: "I occupy the post of remonstrator, yet to this day do not know whether the sacred person is safe—how much more so for the remote and insignificant!"
translations.idiomatic: "I hold the rank of remonstrator, yet still do not know whether Your Majesty is safe—what of the humble officials far below me?"

sentences.zh: 儻群臣不顧君上，罪固當誅；

translations.literal: "If the officials disregard the ruler, punishment is indeed deserved;
translations.idiomatic: "If ministers neglect their sovereign, they deserve punishment—

sentences.zh: 若陛下不恤群臣，於義安在！

translations.literal: but if Your Majesty does not pity the officials, where does righteousness stand!"
translations.idiomatic: but if Your Majesty shows no concern for your ministers, where does duty lie?"

sentences.zh: 夫天下者，高祖、太宗之天下，非北司之天下；

translations.literal: "The realm is the realm of Gaozu and Taizong—not the realm of the northern offices;
translations.idiomatic: "The realm belongs to Gaozu and Taizong—not to the northern offices.

sentences.zh: 天子者，四海九州之天子，非北司之天子。

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven is Son of Heaven to the four seas and nine provinces—not Son of Heaven of the northern offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven reigns over the four seas and nine provinces—not over the eunuch establishment alone."

sentences.zh: 北司未必盡可信，南司未必盡無用。

translations.literal: "The northern offices are not necessarily all trustworthy; the southern offices are not necessarily all useless."
translations.idiomatic: "The eunuchs are not invariably trustworthy; the civil officials are not invariably useless."

sentences.zh: 豈天子與宰相了無關涉，朝臣皆若路人！

translations.literal: "How can the Son of Heaven and the grand councilors have no relation at all, and the court officials all be like passersby on the road!"
translations.idiomatic: "Can the emperor and his grand councilors have no connection at all, with court officials treated like strangers in the street?"

sentences.zh: 如此，恐收復之期，尚勞宸慮，尸祿之士，得以宴安。

translations.literal: "If it is thus, I fear the day of recovery will still burden your sagely thoughts, while officials who hold salaries without work will enjoy ease and peace."
translations.idiomatic: "At this rate, restoring the dynasty will remain an exhausting burden on Your Majesty, while salary-drawers who do no work will live in comfort."

sentences.zh: 臣躬被寵榮，職在裨益，雖遂事不諫，而來者可追。

translations.literal: "I personally have received favor and honor; my duty is to add benefit—though what is done cannot be remonstrated against, what is to come may still be amended."
translations.idiomatic: "I have received imperial favor; my office is to advise. Past errors cannot be undone—but the future can still be set right."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，令孜屏不奏。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Lingzi suppressed it and did not present it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi intercepted the memorial and never forwarded it to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 辛未，矯詔貶昭圖嘉州司戶，遣人沉於蟆頤津，聞者氣塞而莫敢言。

translations.literal: On xinwei, a forged edict demoted Zhaotu to Registrar of Jia Prefecture and sent men to drown him at Ma'yi Ford; those who heard of it choked with rage but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei a forged edict demoted Meng Zhaotu to registrar of Jiazhou and ordered men to drown him at Ma'yi Ford. All who heard it were suffocated with outrage—and none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 鄜延節度使李孝昌、權夏州節度使拓跋思恭屯東渭橋，黃巢遣朱溫拒之。

translations.literal: Li Xiaochang, military commissioner of Fuyan, and Tuo Ba Sigong, acting military commissioner of Xia Prefecture, were encamped at Dongweiqiao Bridge; Huang Chao sent Zhu Wen to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyan commissioner Li Xiaochang and acting Xia commissioner Tuo Ba Sigong encamped at the Eastern Wei Bridge. Huang Chao sent Zhu Wen to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 以義武節度使王處存為東南面行營招討使，以邠寧節度副使朱玫為節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun, military commissioner of Yiwu, was made campaign commander of the Southeastern Field Headquarters; Zhu Mei, deputy military commissioner of Binning, was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun, Yiwu military commissioner, was appointed commander of the southeastern campaign headquarters; Binning deputy commissioner Zhu Mei was promoted to full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八月，己丑夜，星交流如織，或大如杯，至丁酉乃止。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the night of jichou, stars crossed and mingled like woven threads, some as large as cups; this continued until dingyou, when it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the night of jichou, stars crossed like woven threads, some as large as cups, until dingyou, when the spectacle ended.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使支詳遣牙將時溥、陳璠將兵五千入關，討黃巢，二人皆詳所獎拔也。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiang, military commissioner of Wuning, sent his adjutant generals Shi Pu and Chen Fan with five thousand troops into the pass to campaign against Huang Chao. Both men had been promoted and nurtured by Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuning commissioner Zhi Xiang sent adjutants Shi Pu and Chen Fan with five thousand men through the pass against Huang Chao; both were men he had raised.

sentences.zh: 溥至東都，矯稱詳命，召師還與璠合兵，屠河陰，掠鄭州而東。

translations.literal: When Pu reached the eastern capital, he falsely claimed orders from Xiang, recalled the army, joined forces with Fan, slaughtered Heyin, plundered Zhengzhou, and marched east.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern capital, Pu forged orders in Xiang's name, recalled the army, joined Fan, sacked Heyin, plundered Zhengzhou, and marched east.

sentences.zh: 及彭城，詳迎勞，犒賞甚厚。

translations.literal: When they reached Pengcheng, Xiang came out to welcome and reward them with very generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengcheng, Xiang welcomed them with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 溥遣所親說詳曰：「眾心見迫，請公解印以相授。

translations.literal: Pu sent a close associate to tell Xiang, "The troops' will presses upon us; we ask you to surrender your seal and transfer authority."
translations.idiomatic: Pu sent a confidant to tell Xiang, "The men demand it—please surrender your seal."

sentences.zh: 」詳不能制，出居大彭館，溥自知留務。

translations.literal: " Xiang could not control them. He moved out to the Da Peng Inn, and Pu himself took charge of remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Powerless to resist, Xiang moved to the Da Peng Inn while Pu seized control.

sentences.zh: 璠謂溥曰：「支僕射有惠於徐人，不殺，必成後悔。

translations.literal: Fan said to Pu, "Vice Director Zhi has shown kindness to the people of Xu. If we do not kill him, we will surely regret it later."
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Pu, "Vice Director Zhi has done good for Xu. Leave him alive and we'll regret it."

sentences.zh: 」溥不許，送詳歸朝。

translations.literal: " Pu would not agree and sent Xiang back to court.
translations.idiomatic: " Pu refused and sent Xiang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 璠伏甲於七里亭，並其家屬殺之。

translations.literal: Fan hid armed men at Qili Pavilion and killed Xiang together with his entire household.
translations.idiomatic: Fan ambushed Xiang at Qili Pavilion and killed him and his household.

sentences.zh: 詔以溥為武寧留後。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Pu acting military commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Pu acting Wuning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 溥表璠為宿州刺史，璠到官貪虐，溥以都張友代還，殺之。

translations.literal: Pu memorialized making Fan prefect of Suzhou. When Fan took office he was greedy and cruel. Pu sent the commander Zhang You to replace him on his return and killed Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Pu got Fan appointed Suzhou prefect, but Fan proved greedy and cruel. Pu sent commander Zhang You to replace him—and had Fan killed.

sentences.zh: 楊復光奏升蔡州為奉國軍，以秦宗權為防禦使。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang memorialized elevating Caizhou to the Fengguo Army and appointing Qin Zongquan its defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang had Caizhou elevated to the Fengguo Army and Qin Zongquan made its defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壽州屠者王緒與妹夫劉行全聚眾五百，盜據本州，月餘，復陷光州，自稱將軍，有眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: Wang Xu, a butcher of Shouzhou, with his brother-in-law Liu Xingquan gathered five hundred men, seized the prefecture by force, and after more than a month also captured Guangzhou, declaring himself general with more than ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhou butcher Wang Xu and his brother-in-law Liu Xingquan raised five hundred men, seized their home prefecture, and a month later took Guangzhou as well, proclaiming himself a general at the head of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權表為光州刺史。

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan memorialized appointing him prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan had him appointed Guangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 固始縣佐王潮及弟審邽、審知皆以材氣知名，緒以潮為軍正，使典盜糧，閱士卒，信用之。

translations.literal: Wang Chao, an assistant magistrate of Gushi County, and his younger brothers Shen Gui and Shen Zhi were all known for talent and drive. Xu made Chao army rectifier, put him in charge of plundered grain, and had him inspect the troops, trusting him fully.
translations.idiomatic: Gushi assistant Wang Chao and his brothers Shen Gui and Shen Zhi were known for ability and spirit. Xu made Chao army rectifier, put him in charge of loot and troop inspection, and trusted him completely.

sentences.zh: 高潯與黃巢將李詳戰於石橋，潯敗，奔河中，詳乘勝復取華州。

translations.literal: Gao Xun fought Huang Chao's general Li Xiang at Shiqiao. Xun was defeated and fled to Hezhong. Xiang pressed the victory and recovered Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xun fought Li Xiang at Shiqiao, was beaten, and fled to Hezhong. Xiang pressed his advantage and retook Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 巢以詳為華州刺史。

translations.literal: Chao made Xiang prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chao appointed Xiang Hua prefect.

sentences.zh: 以權知夏綏節度使拓跋思恭為節度使。

translations.literal: Tuoba Sigi, who had been acting military commissioner of the Xia-Sui circuit, was formally appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Sigi was confirmed as Xia-Sui commissioner, ending his acting appointment.

sentences.zh: 宗正少卿嗣曹王龜年自南詔還，驃信上表款附，請悉遵詔旨。

translations.literal: Gui Nian, heir prince of Cao and vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, returned from Nanzhao. The Piao Xin submitted a memorial expressing cordial submission and requesting to follow all imperial edicts fully.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cao line Gui Nian returned from Nanzhao. The Nanzhao ruler submitted a loyal memorial pledging full compliance with imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 九月，李孝昌、拓跋思恭與尚讓、朱溫戰於東渭橋，不利，引去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Li Xiaochang and Tuoba Sigi fought Shang Rang and Zhu Wen at East Wei Bridge. The encounter went badly and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Xiaochang and Sigi fought Shang Rang and Zhu Wen at East Wei Bridge, lost, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，高駢與鎮海節度使周寶俱出神策軍，駢以兄事寶。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Pian and Zhou Bao, military commissioner of Zhenhai, had both come from the Shence Army. Pian treated Bao as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian and Zhenhai commissioner Zhou Bao had both served in the Shence Army; Pian treated Bao like an older brother.

sentences.zh: 及駢先貴有功，浸輕之。

translations.literal: When Pian rose first to high rank with merit, he gradually looked down on Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pian rose first to power and glory, he began to look down on Bao.

sentences.zh: 既而封壤相鄰，數爭細故，遂有隙。

translations.literal: Then their jurisdictions bordered each other; they quarreled repeatedly over trifles and gradually grew estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Their territories bordered one another; petty disputes bred a breach between them.

sentences.zh: 駢檄寶入援京師，寶治舟師以俟之，怪其久不行。

translations.literal: Pian issued a dispatch calling on Bao to enter and rescue the capital. Bao prepared a fleet and waited, but was puzzled that Pian did not move for so long.
translations.idiomatic: Pian called on Bao to march north and relieve the capital. Bao readied a fleet and waited—but wondered why Pian never came.

sentences.zh: 訪諸幕客，或曰：「高公幸朝廷多故，有併吞江東之志，聲雲入援，其實未必非圖我也！

translations.literal: Bao consulted his staff. Someone said, "Lord Gao, taking advantage of the court's many troubles, intends to swallow the Jiangdong region. He claims he will come to the rescue, but in truth he may well be plotting against us!"
translations.idiomatic: His staff warned him, "Gao Pian exploits the chaos to aim at Jiangdong. He talks of relieving the capital—but he may be aiming at you."

sentences.zh: 宜為備。

translations.literal: We should prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: You should prepare.

sentences.zh: 」寶未之信，使人覘駢，殊無北上意。

translations.literal: " Bao did not believe it. He sent men to observe Pian and found no sign whatsoever of a northward move.
translations.idiomatic: " Bao did not believe it. Spies reported no sign Pian meant to march north.

sentences.zh: 會駢使人約寶面會瓜洲議軍事，寶遂以言者為然，辭疾不往。

translations.literal: Just then Pian sent envoys inviting Bao to meet face to face at Guazhou to discuss military matters. Bao then believed the warning, pleaded illness, and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian invited Bao to meet at Guazhou, Bao took the warning to heart, pleaded illness, and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 且謂使者曰：「吾非李康，高公復欲作家門功勳以欺朝廷邪？

translations.literal: He also told the envoys, "I am not Li Kang! Does Lord Gao again mean to manufacture family glory and deceive the court?"
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoys, "I'm no Li Kang. Does Gao plan another family triumph to fool the court?"

sentences.zh: 」駢怒，復遣使責寶，「何敢輕侮大臣？

translations.literal: " Pian was furious and again sent envoys to rebuke Bao: "How dare you lightly insult a great minister?"
translations.idiomatic: " Pian sent envoys to rebuke him: "How dare you insult a grand minister?"

sentences.zh: 」寶詬之曰：「彼此夾江為節度使，汝為大臣，我豈坊門卒邪！

translations.literal: " Bao cursed them, saying, "We face each other across the river as military commissioners. You are a great minister—am I some ward gate guard?"
translations.idiomatic: " Bao shot back, "We're equals across the river—commissioners both. Am I some gate guard for you to bully?"

sentences.zh: 」由是遂為深仇。

translations.literal: " From this they became deep enemies.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on they were mortal enemies.

sentences.zh: 駢留東塘百餘日，詔屢趣之，駢上表，托以寶及浙東觀察使劉漢寵將為後患，辛亥，復罷兵還府，其實無赴難心，但欲禳雉集之異耳。

translations.literal: Pian remained at Dongtang for more than a hundred days. Edicts repeatedly urged him onward, but Pian submitted memorials citing Bao and Liu Hanchong, governor of Zhedong, as potential later threats. On xinhai he again demobilized and returned to headquarters. In truth he had no heart to go to the rescue; he only wanted to dispel the omen of gathered pheasants.
translations.idiomatic: Pian lingered at Dongtang for over a hundred days despite repeated imperial orders. He cited Bao and Zhedong governor Liu Hanchong as future threats. On xinhai he disbanded and went home—he never meant to save the capital, only to avert the omen of pheasants gathering.

sentences.zh: 高駢召石鏡鎮將董昌至廣陵，欲與之俱擊黃巢。

translations.literal: Gao Pian summoned Dong Chang, garrison commander of Shijing, to Guangling, intending to join him in attacking Huang Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Pian summoned Shijing commander Dong Chang to Guangling to join him against Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 昌將錢鏐說昌曰：「觀高公無討賊心，不若以扞御鄉里為辭而去之。

translations.literal: Chang's officer Qian Liu persuaded him, saying, "I see that Lord Gao has no heart to suppress the bandits. Better to plead defending our home region and leave him."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu told Chang, "Gao Pian has no heart for fighting rebels. Plead hometown defense and leave."

sentences.zh: 」昌從之，駢聽昌還。

translations.literal: " Chang agreed, and Pian permitted him to return.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang took his advice; Pian let him go.

sentences.zh: 會杭州刺史路審中將之官，行至嘉興，昌自石鏡引兵入杭州，審中懼而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Lu Shenzhong, prefect of Hangzhou, was on his way to take office. When he reached Jiaxing, Chang led troops from Shijing into Hangzhou. Shenzhong, afraid, turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou prefect Lu Shenzhong was en route to office when Chang marched from Shijing into the city at Jiaxing. Shenzhong fled.

sentences.zh: 昌自稱杭州都押牙、知州事，遣將吏請於周寶。

translations.literal: Chang styled himself chief military administrator and acting prefect of Hangzhou and sent officers to request confirmation from Zhou Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang declared himself Hangzhou's chief administrator and acting prefect and asked Zhou Bao for recognition.

sentences.zh: 寶不能制，表為杭州刺史。

translations.literal: Bao could not restrain him and memorialized appointing him prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao could not stop him and had him appointed Hangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 臨海賊杜雄陷台州。

translations.literal: Du Xiong, bandit leader of Linhai, captured Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai bandit Du Xiong took Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，立皇子震為建王。

translations.literal: On xinyou, the emperor's son Zhen was installed as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Prince Zhen was created Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 昭義十將成麟殺高潯，引兵還據潞州。

translations.literal: Cheng Lin, one of the ten Zhao-Yi generals, killed Gao Xun, led the army back, and seized Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao-Yi general Cheng Lin killed Gao Xun, marched back, and held Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天井關戍將孟方立起兵攻麟，殺之。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli, garrison commander of Tianjing Pass, raised troops to attack Cheng Lin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjing Pass garrison commander Meng Fangli rose against Cheng Lin and killed him.

sentences.zh: 方立，刑州人也。

translations.literal: Fangli was a native of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli was from Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 忠武監軍楊復光屯武功。

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang, army supervisor of Zhongwu, encamped at Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu supervisor Yang Fuguang camped at Wugong.

sentences.zh: 永嘉賊朱褒陷溫州。

translations.literal: Zhu Bao, bandit leader of Yongjia, captured Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjia bandit Zhu Bao took Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔行軍司馬李昌言將本軍屯興平。

translations.literal: Li Changyan, campaign marshal of Fengxiang, led the main army to encamp at Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang campaign marshal Li Changyan encamped at Xingping with the main army.

sentences.zh: 時鳳翔倉庫虛竭，犒賞稍薄，糧饋不繼。

translations.literal: At the time Fengxiang's storehouses were exhausted; rewards were somewhat meager and grain supplies did not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang's stores were empty, rewards thin, and grain supplies failing.

sentences.zh: 昌言知府中兵少，因激怒其眾。

translations.literal: Changyan knew the troops in the prefectural seat were few and therefore incited his men to anger.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the capital garrison was weak, Changyan stirred his troops to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，引軍還襲府城。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, he led the army back in a surprise attack on the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he marched back and seized the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋登城與士卒言，其眾皆下馬羅拜曰：「相公誠無負我曹。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian mounted the wall to speak with the troops. They all dismounted, bowed in ranks, and said, "Lord Chancellor, you truly have not wronged us."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian mounted the wall to address them. They dismounted and bowed: "Chancellor, you've never wronged us."

sentences.zh: 」畋曰：「行軍苟能戢兵愛人，為國滅賊，亦可以順守矣。

translations.literal: " Tian said, "If the campaign marshal can restrain the troops and cherish the people, destroy the bandits for the state, he may also hold office rightfully."
translations.idiomatic: " Tian said, "If the marshal keeps order, cares for the people, and destroys the rebels for the state, he may hold command lawfully."

sentences.zh: 」乃以留務委之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon entrusted remaining affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He entrusted remaining affairs to Changyan.

sentences.zh: 即日西赴行在。

translations.literal: That same day he went west to the itinerant court.
translations.idiomatic: That day he went west to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 天平節度使、南面招討使曹全晸與賊戰死，軍中立其兄子存實為留後。

translations.literal: Cao Quanzhen, military commissioner of Tianping and southern campaign commander, died in battle with the bandits. The army installed his elder brother's son Cunshi as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianping commissioner and southern campaign commander Cao Quanzhen was killed fighting rebels; the army made his nephew Cunshi acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙巳，孟楷、朱溫襲鄜、夏二軍於富平，二軍敗，奔歸本道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yisi, Meng Kai and Zhu Wen attacked the Fu and Xia armies at Fuping. Both armies were defeated and fled back to their home circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yisi, Meng Kai and Zhu Wen routed the Fu and Xia armies at Fuping; both fled home.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋至鳳州，累表辭位。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian reached Feng Prefecture and repeatedly submitted memorials resigning his post.
translations.idiomatic: At Feng Prefecture, Zheng Tian repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 詔以畋為太子少傅、分司，以李昌言為鳳翔節度行營招討使。

translations.literal: An edict made Tian Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with a nominal post and Li Changyan campaign commander and military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tian was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent in a nominal post; Li Changyan became Fengxiang campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 以門下侍郎、同平章事裴澈為鄂岳觀察使。

translations.literal: Pei Che, vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor, was made governor of the E-Yue region.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director and councilor Pei Che was made E-Yue governor.

sentences.zh: 加鎮海節度使周寶同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhou Bao, military commissioner of Zhenhai, was additionally made associate grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhai commissioner Zhou Bao joined the grand council.

sentences.zh: 遂昌賊盧約陷處州。

translations.literal: Lu Yue, bandit leader of Suichang, captured Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Suichang bandit Lu Yue took Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，江西將閔勖戍湖南，還，過潭州，逐觀察使李裕，自為留後。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Min Xu, a Jiangxi general who had garrisoned Hunan, returned, passed through Tanzhou, drove out Governor Li Yu, and installed himself as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Hunan garrison general Min Xu of Jiangxi passed through Tanzhou, expelled governor Li Yu, and made himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以感化留後時溥為節度使。

translations.literal: Shi Pu, acting military commissioner of Ganhu, was formally appointed military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Ganhu commissioner Shi Pu was confirmed in office.

sentences.zh: 賜夏州號定難軍。

translations.literal: Xia Prefecture was granted the name Dingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Prefecture was renamed the Dingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 初，高駢鎮荊南，補武陵蠻雷滿為牙將，領蠻軍，從駢至淮南，逃歸，聚眾千人，襲朗州，殺刺史崔翥，詔以滿為朗州留後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gao Pian governed Jingnan, he appointed Lei Man, a Wuling tribesman, as adjutant general to command tribal troops. Man followed Pian to Huainan, then escaped home, gathered a thousand men, raided Lang Prefecture, killed Prefect Cui Zhu, and was appointed acting Lang prefect by edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Pian governed Jingnan, he made Wuling tribesman Lei Man an adjutant commanding tribal forces. Man followed Pian to Huainan, then fled home, raised a thousand men, seized Lang Prefecture, killed prefect Cui Zhu, and was recognized as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 歲中，率三四引兵寇荊南，入其郛，焚掠而去，大為荊人之患。

translations.literal: Within the year he led raids against Jingnan three or four times, entered the outer wall, burned and plundered, then withdrew—a great affliction to the people of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: That year he raided Jingnan three or four times, burning and looting within the walls—a plague on the region.

sentences.zh: 陬溪人周岳嘗與滿獵，爭肉而鬥，欲殺滿，不果。

translations.literal: Zhou Yue of Zouxi had once hunted with Man; they quarreled over meat and fought. Yue tried to kill Man but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue of Zouxi had hunted with Man, fought over the kill, and tried to murder him without success.

sentences.zh: 聞滿據朗州，亦聚眾襲衡州，逐刺史徐顥。

translations.literal: Hearing that Man held Lang Prefecture, he too gathered followers, raided Heng Prefecture, and drove out Prefect Xu Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Man held Langzhou, Yue raised troops, seized Heng Prefecture, and expelled prefect Xu Hao.

sentences.zh: 詔以岳為衡州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yue prefect of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was appointed Heng prefect.

sentences.zh: 石門洞蠻向環亦集夷獠數千攻陷澧州，殺刺史呂自牧，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: Xiang Huan, a Shimen Cave tribesman, also gathered several thousand Yi and Liao warriors, captured Li Prefecture, killed Prefect Lü Zimu, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Shimen Cave tribesman Xiang Huan rallied thousands of tribal warriors, took Li Prefecture, killed prefect Lü Zimu, and declared himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 王鐸以高駢為諸道都統無心討賊，自以身為首相，發憤請行，懇款流涕，至於再三。

translations.literal: Wang Duo, seeing that Gao Pian as overall commander of all circuits had no heart to suppress the bandits, considered himself chief minister and in indignant urgency requested to take the field himself, sincere and tearful, repeatedly pleading.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced Gao Pian would never fight, chief minister Wang Duo begged repeatedly to take the field himself—earnest, weeping, and insistent.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 僖宗惠聖恭定孝皇帝中之上中和二年（

translations.literal: The second year of Zhonghe, middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang, Huishèng Gongding Xiaoxiao (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Zhonghe (middle reign of Emperor Xizong of Tang) (

sentences.zh: 壬寅，公元八八二年）

translations.literal: renyin, corresponding to the year 882 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renyin, 882 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，以王鐸兼中書令，充諸道行營都都統，權知義成節度使，俟罷兵復還政府。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, Wang Duo was additionally made Director of the Secretariat, appointed overall commander of all campaign circuits, and given acting charge of the Yicheng military commission, to return to the central government once the campaign ended.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinhai, Wang Duo became Secretariat Director and overall campaign commander with acting Yicheng commission—a temporary leave from court until the war ended.

sentences.zh: 高駢但領鹽鐵轉運使，罷其都統及諸使。

translations.literal: Gao Pian was left with only the salt and iron transport commission; his overall command and other commissions were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Pian kept only the salt and iron transport post; his supreme command and other titles were stripped.

sentences.zh: 聽王鐸自辟將佐，以太子少師崔安潛為副都統。

translations.literal: Wang Duo was permitted to appoint his own generals and staff, and Cui Anqian, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was made deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Duo could choose his own staff; heir-apparent mentor Cui Anqian became deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以周岌、王重榮為都都統左右司馬，諸葛爽及宣武節度使康實為左右先鋒使，時溥為催遣綱運租賦防遏使，以右神策觀軍容使西門思恭為諸道行營都都監。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Zhou Ji and Wang Chongrong were made left and right marshals of the overall command; Zhuge Shuang and Kang Shi, military commissioner of Xuanwu, were made left and right vanguard commanders; Shi Pu was made commissioner for pressing grain transport, tax collection, and interdiction; and Ximen Sijing, army-observing commissioner of the Right Shence Army, was made overall supervisor of all campaign circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Zhou Ji and Wang Chongrong became left and right marshals; Zhuge Shuang and Xuanwu commissioner Kang Shi became vanguard commanders; Shi Pu oversaw grain, taxes, and supply lines; and Right Shence observer Ximen Sijing became overall campaign supervisor.

sentences.zh: 又以王處存、李孝昌、拓跋思恭為京城東北西面都統，以楊復光為南面行營都監使。

translations.literal: Wang Chucun, Li Xiaochang, and Tuoba Sigi were also made overall commanders of the northeast and west of the capital, and Yang Fuguang was made southern campaign supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun, Xiaochang, and Sigi took the capital's northeast and west; Fuguang supervised the southern camp.

sentences.zh: 又以中書舍人鄭昌圖為義成節度行軍司馬，給事中鄭畯為判官，直弘文館王摶為推官，司勳員外郎裴贄為掌書記。

translations.literal: Zheng Changtu, Secretariat drafting officer, was made Yicheng campaign marshal; Zheng Jun, a reviewing censor, was made administrative aide; Wang Tuan, scholar on duty at the Hongwen Institute, was made investigating officer; and Pei Zhi, outer-office secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, was made chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat drafter Zheng Changtu became Yicheng campaign marshal; censor Zheng Jun became aide; Hongwen scholar Wang Tuan became investigator; and personnel secretary Pei Zhi became chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 昌圖，從讜之從祖兄弟；

translations.literal: Changtu was a cousin of Congdan on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Changtu was a cousin of Congdan.

sentences.zh: 畯，畋之弟；

translations.literal: Jun was Tian's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was Tian's brother.

sentences.zh: 摶，璵之曾孫；

translations.literal: Tuan was a great-grandson of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan was Yu's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 贄，坦之子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was Tan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was Tan's son.

sentences.zh: 又以陝虢觀察使王重盈為東面都供軍使。

translations.literal: Wang Chongying, governor of Shan-Guo, was also made eastern overall supply commissioner for the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shan-Guo governor Wang Chongying became eastern supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 重盈，重榮之兄也。

translations.literal: Chongying was Chongrong's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Chongying was Chongrong's brother.

sentences.zh: 黃巢以朱溫為同州刺史，令溫自取之。

translations.literal: Huang Chao made Zhu Wen prefect of Tong Prefecture and ordered Wen to take it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chao made Zhu Wen Tong prefect and told him to take the post himself.

sentences.zh: 二月，同州刺史米誠奔河中，溫遂據之。

translations.literal: In the second month, Mi Cheng, prefect of Tong Prefecture, fled to Hezhong, and Wen thereupon seized it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Tong prefect Mi Cheng fled to Hezhong; Wen seized the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以太子少傅、分司鄭畋為司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事，召詣行在，軍務一以咨之。

translations.literal: On jimao, Zheng Tian, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent in a nominal post, was made Minister of Works, concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery and associate grand councilor, summoned to the itinerant court, and consulted on all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, nominal heir-apparent mentor Zheng Tian became Minister of Works, vice director, and councilor, summoned to the emperor's camp with full authority over military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以王鐸兼判戶部事。

translations.literal: Wang Duo was additionally assigned to oversee Ministry of Revenue affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo also took charge of revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 朱溫寇河中，王重榮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen raided Hezhong and was defeated by Wang Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen raided Hezhong; Wang Chongrong beat him back.

sentences.zh: 以李昌言為京城西面都統，朱玫為河南都統。

translations.literal: Li Changyan was made overall commander of the western capital and Zhu Mei overall commander of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changyan took the capital's west; Zhu Mei took Henan.

sentences.zh: 涇原節度使胡公素薨，軍中請命於都統王鐸，承製以大將張鈞為留後。

translations.literal: Hu Gongsu, military commissioner of Jingyuan, died. The army asked Wang Duo, overall commander, for orders, and by provisional edict the senior general Zhang Jun was made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan commissioner Hu Gongsu died. The army appealed to overall commander Wang Duo, who provisionally named senior general Zhang Jun acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 李克用寇蔚州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong raided You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong raided You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，振武節度使契苾璋奏與天德、大同共討克用。

translations.literal: In the third month, Qibi Zhang, military commissioner of Zhenwu, memorialized that he would join Tiande and Datong in a joint campaign against Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhenwu commissioner Qibi Zhang reported a joint campaign with Tiande and Datong against Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 詔鄭從讜與相知應接。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zheng Congdan to know and coordinate mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Zheng Congdan to coordinate mutual support.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄多遣人歷縣鎮詗事，謂之尋事人，所至多所求取。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan frequently sent men through counties and garrisons to inquire into affairs; they were called "search-for-trouble men" and everywhere they went they made many demands.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan sent "search-for-trouble men" through every county and garrison to spy and extort.

sentences.zh: 有二人過資陽鎮，獨無所求。

translations.literal: Two of them passed through Ziyang garrison and alone made no demands.
translations.idiomatic: Two passed through Ziyang garrison and asked for nothing.

sentences.zh: 鎮將謝弘讓邀之，不至。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Xie Hongrang invited them but they would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Xie Hongrang invited them; they refused.

sentences.zh: 自疑有罪，夜，亡入群盜中。

translations.literal: Hongrang suspected himself guilty; that night he fled and joined a band of outlaws.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful he was guilty of something, Hongrang fled by night and joined the bandits.

sentences.zh: 明旦，二人去，弘讓實無罪也。

translations.literal: At daybreak the next day, the two men left; Hongrang had in fact committed no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Come dawn the next day, the two men departed; Hongrang had done nothing wrong after all.

sentences.zh: 捕盜使楊遷誘弘讓出首而執以送使，雲討擊擒獲，以求功。

translations.literal: Bandit-capture envoy Yang Qian lured Hongrang into surrendering himself, then seized him and sent him in as a prisoner, claiming he had been captured in pursuit, in order to seek credit.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit-capture envoy Yang Qian tricked Hongrang into turning himself in, then arrested him and reported a capture in the field to claim credit.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄不之問，杖弘讓脊二十，釘於西城二七日，煎油潑之，又以膠麻掣其瘡，備極慘酷，見者冤之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan made no inquiry; he had Hongrang beaten twenty blows on the back, nailed up at the west gate for fourteen days, had boiling oil poured over him, and further pulled his wounds with sticky hemp paste—cruelty to the utmost; those who saw it deemed him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan never looked into the matter. Hongrang was flogged twenty times on the back, nailed to the west gate for fourteen days, scalded with boiling oil, and had his wounds torn open with sticky hemp paste—torture as brutal as any could be. All who witnessed it called it an outrage.

sentences.zh: 又有邛州牙官阡能，因公事違期，避杖，亡命為盜。

translations.literal: There was also Qian Neng, a garrison officer of Qiong Prefecture; because he missed a deadline on official business and wished to avoid the rod, he fled and became a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Qian Neng, a garrison officer at Qiong Prefecture, who missed a deadline on official business, fled to escape the lash, and turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 楊遷復誘之，能方出首，聞弘讓之冤，大罵楊遷，發憤為盜，驅掠良民，不從者舉家殺之。

translations.literal: Yang Qian again lured him; Neng had just surrendered himself when, hearing of Hongrang's injustice, he cursed Yang Qian bitterly, gave vent to his rage as a bandit, drove the people to plunder, and killed whole families of those who would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qian tricked him again. Neng had just turned himself in when he heard how Hongrang had been wronged. He cursed Yang Qian and, in fury, took up banditry again—driving raids against civilians and slaughtering entire families of those who resisted.

sentences.zh: 逾月，眾至萬人，立部伍，署職級，橫行邛、雅二州間，攻陷城邑，所過塗地。

translations.literal: Within a month his followers reached ten thousand; he established units and ranks, ranged between Qiong and Ya Prefectures, stormed and seized towns, and wherever they passed they left the ground smeared with blood.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month his force swelled to ten thousand. He organized ranks and commands, roamed between Qiong and Ya, and stormed towns wherever he went, leaving devastation in his wake.

sentences.zh: 先是，蜀中少盜賊，自是紛紛競起，州縣不能制，敬瑄遣牙將楊行遷將三千人，胡洪略、莫匡時各將二千人以討之。

translations.literal: Previously bandits had been few in Shu; from this time they rose in swarms, and counties and prefectures could not control them. Jingxuan sent aide-general Yang Xingqian with three thousand men, and Hu Honglue and Mo Kuangshi each with two thousand, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry had once been rare in Shu; now it erupted everywhere, beyond what local officials could handle. Jingxuan sent aide-general Yang Xingqian with three thousand troops, and Hu Honglue and Mo Kuangshi each with two thousand, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 以右神策將軍齊克儉為左右神策軍內外八鎮兼博野、奉天節度使。

translations.literal: Right Shence Army general Qi Kejian was appointed commander of the eight garrisons inside and outside the Left and Right Shence Armies, and concurrently military commissioner of Boye and Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Kejian, Right Shence Army general, was made commander of the eight garrisons of the Left and Right Shence Armies, and concurrently military commissioner of Boye and Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 賜鄜坊軍號保大。

translations.literal: The Zhe-Fang army was granted the name Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe-Fang army received the designation Baoda.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，加陳敬瑄兼侍中。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Chen Jingxuan was further appointed concurrent Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiawu, Chen Jingxuan was also made Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 赫連鐸、李可舉與李克用戰，不利。

translations.literal: Helian Duo and Li Keju fought Li Keyong and fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo and Li Keju fought Li Keyong and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 初，高駢好神仙，有方士呂用之坐妖黨，亡命歸駢，駢厚待之，補以軍職。

translations.literal: Initially, Gao Pian loved immortals and transcendents; there was a Taoist adept named Lv Yongzhi who, convicted as an entrant in occult factions, fled as a refugee to Pian; Pian treated him generously and appointed him to a military post.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian had long been devoted to immortals and transcendents. The Taoist adept Lv Yongzhi, condemned for membership in an occult faction, fled to Pian's service. Pian welcomed him warmly and gave him a military commission.

sentences.zh: 用之，鄱陽茶商之子也，久客廣陵，熟其人情，爐鼎之暇，頗言公私利病，駢愈奇之，稍加信任。

translations.literal: Yongzhi was the son of a tea merchant of Poyang; he had long sojourned at Guangling and knew its human affairs well; in idle moments between furnace and cauldron he often spoke of public and private gains and losses; Pian found him ever stranger and gradually extended trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi was a Poyang tea merchant's son who had lived in Guangling for years and knew its people well. Between his alchemical labors he often discussed matters of public and private concern; Pian grew ever more fascinated and began to trust him.

sentences.zh: 駢舊將梁纘、陳珙、馮綬、董瑾、俞公楚、姚歸禮素為駢所厚，用之欲專權，浸以計去之。

translations.literal: Pian's old generals—Liang Zuan, Chen Gong, Feng Shou, Dong Jin, Yu Gongchu, and Yao Guili—had long been favored by him; Yongzhi wished to monopolize power and gradually plotted by stratagem to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Pian's veteran generals—Liang Zuan, Chen Gong, Feng Shou, Dong Jin, Yu Gongchu, and Yao Guili—had long enjoyed his favor. Yongzhi sought sole power and set out by degrees to remove them.

sentences.zh: 駢遂奪纘兵，族珙家，綬、瑾、公楚、歸禮鹹見疏。

translations.literal: Pian then stripped Zuan of his troops, exterminated Gong's clan, and Shou, Jin, Gongchu, and Guili all alike grew estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Pian stripped Liang Zuan of his command, executed Chen Gong's entire clan, and Feng Shou, Dong Jin, Yu Gongchu, and Yao Guili were all in turn pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 用之又引其黨張守一、諸葛殷共蠱惑駢。

translations.literal: Yongzhi also brought in his associates Zhang Shouyi and Zhuge Yin jointly to bewitch Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi then introduced his cronies Zhang Shouyi and Zhuge Yin to beguile Pian together.

sentences.zh: 守一本滄、景村民，以術干駢，無所遇，窮困甚，用之謂曰：「但與吾同心，勿憂不富貴。

translations.literal: Shouyi was originally a villager of Cang and Jing; he sought Pian with arts of wizardry but found no favor, and was extremely destitute; Yongzhi said to him, "Only join your heart with mine; do not worry that riches and honor will not come."
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi was a peasant from Cang and Jing who had tried to impress Pian with occult arts and found only poverty. Yongzhi told him, "Stand with me and you need never fear lacking wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 」遂薦於駢，駢寵待埒於用之。

translations.literal: He then recommended him to Pian, and Pian favored and treated him on a par with Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Shouyi to Pian, who treated him with the same favor as Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 殷始自鄱陽來，用之先言於駢曰：「玉皇以公職事繁重，輟左右尊神一人佐公為理，公善遇之。

translations.literal: Yin had just come from Poyang; Yongzhi first spoke to Pian, saying, "The Jade Emperor, because your official duties are heavy, has released one honored spirit from his side to assist you in governance; treat him well."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin arrived from Poyang, Yongzhi told Pian first, "The Jade Emperor finds your duties too heavy and has sent one of the august spirits at his side to assist you. Treat him well."

sentences.zh: 欲其久留，亦可縻以人間重職。

translations.literal: If you wish him to stay long, you may also tether him with weighty earthly posts.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish him to remain, you may bind him here with an important earthly office.

sentences.zh: 」明日，殷謁見，詭辯風生，駢以為神，補鹽鐵劇職。

translations.literal: The next day Yin presented himself; his sophistry sprang like wind; Pian took him for a spirit and assigned him to the weighty salt-and-iron office.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yin appeared before him, speaking with dazzling but slippery eloquence. Pian took him for a divine being and gave him a high post in the salt-and-iron bureau.

sentences.zh: 駢嚴潔，甥侄輩未嘗得接坐。

translations.literal: Pian was stern and fastidious; his nephews and nieces had never been granted seats beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was austere and reserved; even his nephews and nieces were never allowed to sit with him.

sentences.zh: 殷病風疽，搔捫不替手，膿血滿爪，駢獨與之同席促膝，傳杯器而食。

translations.literal: Yin suffered from wind-sores; he scratched and rubbed without cease, pus and blood filling his fingernails; Pian alone shared a mat knee to knee with him, passing cups and vessels as they ate.
translations.idiomatic: Yin suffered from festering sores and scratched them incessantly, his nails caked with pus and blood. Pian alone sat knee to knee with him at meals, sharing cups and dishes from the same tableware.

sentences.zh: 左右以為言，駢曰：「神仙以此試人耳！

translations.literal: Those around him spoke of it; Pian said, "Immortals use this to test men!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants remonstrated, but Pian said, "Immortals test men in just this way!"

sentences.zh: 」駢有畜犬，聞其腥穢，多來近之。

translations.literal: Pian kept dogs; smelling his foul stench, many came near him.
translations.idiomatic: Pian kept dogs that, drawn by the stench, would often gather around Yin.

sentences.zh: 駢怪之，殷笑曰：「殷嘗於玉皇前見之，別來數百年，猶相識。

translations.literal: Pian thought it strange; Yin laughed and said, "Yin once saw them before the Jade Emperor; though we have parted these several hundred years, we still recognize one another."
translations.idiomatic: Pian found this odd. Yin laughed and said, "I once saw these dogs before the Jade Emperor. Though centuries have passed since we parted, we still know each other."

sentences.zh: 」駢與鄭畋有隙，用之謂駢曰：「宰相有遣劍客來刺公者，今夕至矣！

translations.literal: Pian had a rift with Zheng Tian; Yongzhi said to Pian, "The chief minister has sent swordsmen to assassinate you; they will arrive tonight!"
translations.idiomatic: Pian was at odds with Chief Minister Zheng Tian. Yongzhi told him, "The chief minister has sent assassins—they arrive tonight!"

sentences.zh: 」駢大懼，問計安出。

translations.literal: Pian was greatly afraid and asked whence counsel might come.
translations.idiomatic: Pian was terrified and asked what could be done.

sentences.zh: 用之曰：「張先生嘗學斯術，可以御之。

translations.literal: Yongzhi said, "Master Zhang once studied this art and can repel them."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi said, "Master Zhang has studied this art and can defend against them."

sentences.zh: 」駢請於守一，守一許諾。

translations.literal: Pian asked Shouyi, and Shouyi assented.
translations.idiomatic: Pian appealed to Shouyi, who agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃使駢衣婦人之服，潛於它室，而守一代居駢寢榻中，夜擲銅器於階，令鏗然有聲。

translations.literal: He then had Pian don women's clothes and hide in another chamber, while Shouyi took Pian's place in bed; at night he threw bronze vessels onto the steps so they rang sharply.
translations.idiomatic: They dressed Pian in women's clothes and hid him in another room while Shouyi occupied his bed. That night Shouyi hurled bronze vessels onto the steps with a great clamor.

sentences.zh: 又密以囊盛彘血，灑於庭宇，如格鬥之狀。

translations.literal: He also secretly filled a bag with pig's blood and sprinkled it in the courtyard as though from a struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he filled a bag with pig's blood and splashed it across the courtyard as if from a fight.

sentences.zh: 及旦，笑謂駢曰：「幾落奴手！

translations.literal: At dawn he laughed and said to Pian, "You nearly fell into that scoundrel's hands!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told Pian with a laugh, "You nearly fell into that villain's hands!"

sentences.zh: 」駢泣謝曰：「先生於駢，乃更生之惠也！

translations.literal: Pian wept and thanked him, saying, "Master, to Pian this is the kindness of renewed life!"
translations.idiomatic: Pian wept and thanked him: "Master, you have given me life anew!"

sentences.zh: 」厚酬以金寶。

translations.literal: He richly rewarded him with gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him lavishly in gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 有蕭勝者，賂用之，求鹽城監，駢有難色，用之曰：「用之非為勝也，近得上仙書雲，有寶劍在鹽城井中，須一靈官取之。

translations.literal: There was one Xiao Sheng who bribed Yongzhi to seek the post of salt-market superintendent at Yancheng; Pian looked reluctant; Yongzhi said, "It is not for Sheng that Yongzhi acts; recently I received a letter from a superior immortal saying there is a treasured sword in the Yancheng well, and a spirit-officer must fetch it."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xiao Sheng bribed Yongzhi for the post of superintendent at the Yancheng salt market. Pian hesitated, but Yongzhi said, "This is not for Xiao Sheng's sake. I have just received a letter from a superior immortal saying a magic sword lies in the Yancheng well and must be retrieved by a spirit-officer."

sentences.zh: 以勝上仙左右之人，欲使取劍耳。

translations.literal: Because Sheng is one near to a superior immortal, I wish him only to fetch the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng is a man from the retinue of a superior immortal—I merely want him to retrieve the sword.

sentences.zh: 」駢乃許之。

translations.literal: Pian then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Pian agreed.

sentences.zh: 勝至監數月，函一銅匕首以獻，用之見，稽首曰：「此北帝所佩，得之，則百里之內五兵不能犯。

translations.literal: After several months at the post Sheng submitted in a case a bronze dagger; when Yongzhi saw it he kowtowed and said, "This was worn by the Northern Emperor; obtaining it, within a hundred li no weapon of war can harm."
translations.idiomatic: After months at the post, Xiao Sheng presented a boxed bronze dagger. Yongzhi kowtowed upon seeing it and said, "This is the sword the Northern Emperor wore. Whoever holds it cannot be harmed by any weapon within a hundred li."

sentences.zh: 」駢乃飾以珠玉，常置坐隅。

translations.literal: Pian then adorned it with pearls and jade and always kept it at the corner of his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Pian had it adorned with pearls and jade and kept it always at his side.

sentences.zh: 用之自謂磻溪真君，謂守一乃赤松子，殷乃葛將軍，勝乃秦穆公之婿也。

translations.literal: Yongzhi called himself the True Lord of Panxi, called Shouyi the Red Pine Master, Yin General Ge, and Sheng the son-in-law of Duke Mu of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi claimed to be the True Lord of Panxi, declared Shouyi the immortal Red Pine, Yin General Ge, and Sheng the son-in-law of Duke Mu of Qin.

sentences.zh: 用之又刻青石為奇字云：「玉皇授白雲先生高駢。

translations.literal: Yongzhi also carved on blue stone strange characters reading, "The Jade Emperor invests Cloud-White Master Gao Pian."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi also had strange characters carved on blue stone: "The Jade Emperor invests Cloud-White Master Gao Pian."

sentences.zh: 」密令左右置道院香案。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered attendants to place it on the incense table in the Taoist abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly had his attendants place it on the incense table in the Taoist abbey.

sentences.zh: 駢得之，驚喜。

translations.literal: Pian obtained it and was startled and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Pian found it and was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 用之曰：「玉皇以公焚修功著，將補真官，計鸞鶴不日當降此際。

translations.literal: Yongzhi said, "The Jade Emperor, because your merits in burning incense and cultivation are outstanding, will appoint you to a transcendent office; surely cranes and phoenixes will soon descend upon this place."
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi said, "The Jade Emperor sees your dedication in incense and cultivation and will appoint you to a transcendent office. Cranes and phoenixes should descend here any day now."

sentences.zh: 用之等謫限亦滿，必得陪幢節，同歸上清耳！

translations.literal: Our terms of exile will also be fulfilled; we are sure to escort the banner-and-peacock finery and return together to Upper Clarity!
translations.idiomatic: Our term of exile will soon end—we shall surely escort your celestial banners home together to Upper Clarity!

sentences.zh: 」是後，駢於道院庭中刻木鶴，時著羽服跨之，日夕齋醮，煉金燒丹，費以巨萬計。

translations.literal: After this, in the abbey courtyard Pian carved a wooden crane and sometimes put on feather robes and straddled it; morning and evening he performed fasting rites and alchemical elixirs were refined, costs running to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Pian had a wooden crane carved in the abbey courtyard, sometimes donned feather robes and mounted it, and spent morning and evening in fasting rites and elixir-making at a cost of tens of thousands of strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 用之微時，依止江陽后土廟，舉動祈禱。

translations.literal: When Yongzhi was lowly he had attached himself to the Queen Earth temple at Jiangyang, praying in every action.
translations.idiomatic: In his humble days Yongzhi had lodged at the Queen Earth temple in Jiangyang and prayed over everything he did.

sentences.zh: 及得志，白駢崇大其廟，極江南工材之選，每軍旅大事，以少牢禱之。

translations.literal: When he rose to power he had Pian enlarge and exalt that temple, choosing the finest craftsmen and materials of Jiangnan; on every great military matter he offered the shao-lao sacrifice in prayer.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he persuaded Pian to rebuild and enlarge the temple with the finest craftsmen and materials in Jiangnan. Before every major military undertaking he offered the shao-lao sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 用之又言神仙好樓居，說駢作迎仙樓，費十五萬緡。

translations.literal: Yongzhi also said immortals love dwelling in towers; he persuaded Pian to build a Welcome-the-Immortals Tower at a cost of one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi also claimed that immortals prefer living in towers and persuaded Pian to build a Welcome-the-Immortals Tower at a cost of one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 又作延和閣，高八丈。

translations.literal: He also built the Yanhe Pavilion, eight zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Yanhe Pavilion, eighty feet high.

sentences.zh: 用之每對駢呵叱風雨，仰揖空際，雲有神仙過雲表。

translations.literal: Whenever Yongzhi faced Pian he would shout at wind and rain, bow toward the empty sky, and say immortals were passing above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In Pian's presence Yongzhi would shout commands at the wind and rain, bow toward the sky, and claim that immortals were passing overhead.

sentences.zh: 駢輒隨而拜之。

translations.literal: Pian would then follow and bow to them.
translations.idiomatic: Pian would bow along with him.

sentences.zh: 然常厚賂駢左右，使伺駢動靜，共為欺罔，駢不之寤。

translations.literal: Yet he constantly bribed Pian's attendants to watch Pian's movements and join in deceit together; Pian never awakened to it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile he bribed Pian's attendants to report his every move, and together they ran the whole charade—Pian never caught on.

sentences.zh: 左右小有異議者，輒為用之陷死不旋踵，但潛撫膺鳴指，口不敢言。

translations.literal: Attendants who voiced the slightest dissent were at once framed by Yongzhi and put to death without delay; they could only secretly clench their breasts and click their fingers, not daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Any attendant who voiced the slightest dissent was framed and executed at once. The rest could only clutch their chests and click their tongues in silence.

sentences.zh: 駢倚用之如左右手，公私大小之事皆決於用之，退賢進不肖，淫刑濫賞，駢之政事於是大壞矣！

translations.literal: Pian relied on Yongzhi as on right hand and left; public and private affairs great and small were all decided by Yongzhi; worthy men were pushed aside and unworthy advanced; punishments ran wild and rewards were lavished heedlessly—and Pian's governance was thereby greatly ruined!
translations.idiomatic: Pian leaned on Yongzhi as on his right hand; great and small, public and private, all passed through Yongzhi's judgment. Worthy men were pushed aside and fools promoted; punishments multiplied and rewards were showered without measure—and Pian's administration collapsed.

sentences.zh: 用之知上下怨憤，恐有竊發，請置巡察使。

translations.literal: Yongzhi knew that resentment ran high above and below and feared secret outbreaks; he requested the establishment of patrol inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi knew resentment ran high at every level and feared a secret uprising; he asked to establish patrol inspectors.

sentences.zh: 駢即以用之領之，募險獪者百餘人，縱橫閭巷間，謂之「察子」，民間呵妻詈子，靡不知之。

translations.literal: Pian immediately put Yongzhi in charge; over a hundred crafty and cunning men were recruited to range through lanes and alleys; they were called "watchlings"; if in households men scolded wives or cursed children, nothing was unknown to them.
translations.idiomatic: Pian put Yongzhi in charge. He recruited more than a hundred sharp and unscrupulous men to roam every lane and alley—the "watchlings." Not a harsh word between husband and wife escaped their notice.

sentences.zh: 用之欲奪人貨財，掠人婦女，輒誣以叛逆，搒掠取服，殺其人而取之，所破滅者數百家，道路以目，將吏士民雖家居，皆重足屏氣。

translations.literal: When Yongzhi wished to seize others' goods and abduct women, he would frame them for treason, beat them until they confessed, kill the person and take the property; families destroyed numbered in the hundreds; people exchanged glances on the roads; generals, officials, gentry, and commoners even at home all walked on tiptoe and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yongzhi wanted someone's property or a man's wife, he framed the victim for treason, tortured a confession out of him, killed him, and seized everything. Hundreds of families were destroyed. People exchanged fearful glances in the streets; soldiers, officials, and commoners alike tread softly even at home and barely dared to breathe.

sentences.zh: 用之又欲以兵威脅制諸將，請選募諸軍驍勇之士二萬人，號左、右莫邪都。

translations.literal: Yongzhi also wished to threaten and control the generals by military might; he requested selection and recruitment of twenty thousand stalwart warriors from all armies, titled the Left and Right Moye Divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi also sought to intimidate the generals with military force and asked to recruit twenty thousand elite warriors from every army, called the Left and Right Moye Divisions.

sentences.zh: 駢即以張守一及用之為左、右莫邪軍使，署置將吏如帥府，器械精利，衣裝華潔，每出入，導從近千人。

translations.literal: Pian at once made Zhang Shouyi and Yongzhi Left and Right Moye army commissioners; officers and clerks were appointed as at a headquarters; weapons were keen and fine, dress splendid and glossy; each time they went out or in, their escorts numbered nearly a thousand.
